title.zh: 卷一百二十五 列傳第十三 徐達 常遇春
title.en: Volume 125 Biographies 13: Xu Da, Chang Yuchun
title.raw: 卷一百二十五 列傳第十三 徐達 常遇春 Volume 125 Biographies 13: Xu Da, Chang Yuchun

sentences.zh: 徐達 常遇春

translations.literal: Xu Da; Chang Yuchun
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da and Chang Yuchun

sentences.zh: 徐達，字天德，濠人，世業農。

translations.literal: Xu Da, style name Tiande, was a man of Hao; his family for generations practiced agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da, whose style name was Tiande, came from Hao; his family had farmed there for generations.

sentences.zh: 達少有大志，長身高顴，剛毅武勇。

translations.literal: From youth Da had great ambition; when grown he was tall with high cheekbones, firm, resolute, martial, and brave.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Xu Da harbored great ambitions; as a man he was tall, with prominent cheekbones, and was resolute, martial, and fearless.

sentences.zh: 太祖之為郭子興部帥也，達時年二十二，往從之，一見語合。

translations.literal: When the Founder was a division commander under Guo Zixing, Da was then twenty-two; he went to follow him, and at first meeting their words accorded.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder was still a division commander under Guo Zixing, Xu Da was twenty-two; he went to join him, and from their first meeting they were in perfect accord.

sentences.zh: 及太祖南略定遠，帥二十四人往，達首與焉。

translations.literal: When the Founder marched south to seize Dingyuan, he led twenty-four men to go; Da was foremost among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder marched south to take Dingyuan, he led twenty-four men on the expedition, and Xu Da was among the first to go.

sentences.zh: 尋從破元兵於滁州澗，從取和州，子興授達鎮撫。

translations.literal: Soon he followed in defeating Yuan troops at Chuzhou Ravine, followed in taking Hezhou, and Zixing appointed Da as Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed the Founder in defeating Yuan forces at Chuzhou Ravine and in capturing Hezhou; Guo Zixing then appointed Xu Da Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 子興執孫德崖，德崖軍亦執太祖，達挺身詣德崖軍請代，太祖乃得歸，達亦獲免。

translations.literal: Zixing seized Sun Decai, and Decai's army also seized the Founder; Da advanced his person to Decai's army to request substitution, whereupon the Founder was able to return, and Da also obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Zixing seized Sun Decai, Sun's troops seized the Founder in turn; Xu Da went alone to Sun's camp and offered to take his place, so the Founder was released—and Xu Da was spared as well.

sentences.zh: 從渡江，拔採石，取太平，與常遇春皆為軍鋒冠。

translations.literal: He followed in crossing the river, captured Caishi, took Taiping, and with Chang Yuchun both were foremost among the army vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Founder across the Yangzi, captured Caishi and Taiping, and he and Chang Yuchun ranked first among the army's vanguard.

sentences.zh: 從破擒元將陳野先，別將兵取溧陽、溧水，從下集慶。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating and capturing the Yuan general Chen Yexian, separately led troops to take Liyang and Lishui, and followed in reducing Jiqing.
translations.idiomatic: He helped defeat and capture the Yuan general Chen Yexian, led a separate force to take Liyang and Lishui, and took part in the reduction of Jiqing.

sentences.zh: 太祖身居守，而命達為大將，帥諸軍東攻鎮江，拔之。

translations.literal: The Founder himself remained on garrison duty, while appointing Da as great general to command the armies in attacking Zhenjiang to the east; they captured it.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder stayed behind to hold the base while appointing Xu Da grand general to lead the armies east against Zhenjiang, which they captured.

sentences.zh: 號令明肅，城中宴然。

translations.literal: Orders and prohibitions were clear and strict; within the city all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: His orders were clear and discipline strict, and the city remained calm and orderly.

sentences.zh: 授淮興翼統軍元帥。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Huai-Xing Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commander-in-chief of the Huai-Xing wing.

sentences.zh: 時張士誠已據常州，挾江東叛將陳保二以舟師攻鎮江。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Shicheng already held Changzhou; relying on the Jiangdong rebel general Chen Bao'er, he used a fleet to attack Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng already held Changzhou and, with the Jiangdong rebel Chen Bao'er's fleet, attacked Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 達敗之于龍潭，遂請益兵以圍常州。

translations.literal: Da defeated them at Longtan, then requested additional troops to besiege Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da defeated them at Longtan and then asked for reinforcements to besiege Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 士誠遣將來援。

translations.literal: Shicheng dispatched generals to come to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng sent generals to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 達以敵狡而銳，未易力取，乃離城設二伏以待，別遣將王均用為奇兵，而自督軍戰。

translations.literal: Da judged the enemy crafty and sharp, not easy to take by force; he therefore left the city and set two ambushes to wait, separately sent the general Wang Junyong as surprise troops, and himself supervised the army in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Judging the enemy crafty and fierce and not easy to overpower head-on, Xu Da drew off from the city, laid two ambushes, sent Wang Junyong with a flanking force, and personally led the main fight.

sentences.zh: 敵退走遇伏，大敗之，獲其張、湯二將，進圍常州。

translations.literal: The enemy retreated in flight and met the ambushes; he utterly defeated them and captured their two generals Zhang and Tang, then advanced to besiege Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fell back into the ambushes and was routed; Xu Da captured two of their generals, surnamed Zhang and Tang, and pressed the siege of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年克之。

translations.literal: The next year he captured it.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took the city.

sentences.zh: 進僉樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 繼克甯國，徇宜興，使前鋒趙德勝下常熟，擒士誠弟士德。

translations.literal: He next captured Ningguo, marched through Yixing, and had the vanguard Zhao Desheng reduce Changshu, capturing Shicheng's younger brother Shide.
translations.idiomatic: He next took Ningguo, swept through Yixing, and had the vanguard Zhao Desheng seize Changshu and capture Zhang Shicheng's brother Shide.

sentences.zh: 明年復攻宜興，克之。

translations.literal: The next year he again attacked Yixing and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he attacked Yixing again and captured it.

sentences.zh: 太祖自將攻婺州，命達留守應天，別遣兵襲破天完將趙普勝，復池州。

translations.literal: The Founder personally led troops to attack Wuzhou, ordered Da to remain on garrison at Yingtian, and separately sent troops in a surprise attack to defeat the Tianwan general Zhao Pusheng and recover Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founder led the assault on Wuzhou in person, he left Xu Da to hold Yingtian and sent another force to rout the Tianwan general Zhao Pusheng and recover Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 遷奉國上將軍、同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Upholds the State and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Upholds the State and vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 進攻安慶，自無為陸行，夜掩浮山寨，破普勝部將于青山，遂克潛山。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Anqing, he marched by land from Wuwei, by night stormed Fushan Stockade, defeated Pusheng's subordinate general at Qingshan, and thereby captured Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Marching overland from Wuwei against Anqing, he stormed Fushan Stockade by night, routed one of Zhao Pusheng's lieutenants at Qingshan, and took Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 還鎮池州，與遇春設伏，敗陳友諒軍于九華山下，斬首萬人，生擒三千人。

translations.literal: Returning to garrison Chizhou, he and Yuchun set an ambush and defeated Chen Youliang's army below Mount Jiuhua, beheading ten thousand and capturing three thousand alive.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Chizhou he and Chang Yuchun laid an ambush and routed Chen Youliang's army below Mount Jiuhua, killing ten thousand men and taking three thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 遇春曰：「此勁旅也，不殺為後患。」

translations.literal: Yuchun said: "These are crack troops; if not killed they will be a later calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun said, "These are crack troops—if we do not kill them they will trouble us later.

sentences.zh: 達不可，乃以狀聞。

translations.literal: Da would not agree and therefore reported the matter in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da refused and reported the matter to the Founder.

sentences.zh: 而遇春先以夜坑其人過半，太祖不懌，悉縱遣餘眾。

translations.literal: But Yuchun had already by night buried alive more than half of them; the Founder was displeased and released and sent away all the remainder.
translations.idiomatic: But Chang Yuchun had already buried more than half the prisoners alive by night; the Founder was displeased and ordered the rest set free.

sentences.zh: 於是始命達盡護諸將。

translations.literal: Thereupon he first ordered Da to oversee all the generals in full.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Founder put all the generals under Xu Da's overall command.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒犯龍江，達軍南門外，與諸將力戰破之，追及之慈湖，焚其舟。

translations.literal: Chen Youliang invaded Longjiang; Da's army was outside the south gate; with the generals he fought fiercely and defeated them, pursued them to Cihu, and burned their boats.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang attacked Longjiang, Xu Da held the south gate, fought the invaders off with the other generals, pursued them to Cihu, and burned their fleet.

sentences.zh: 明年，從伐漢，取江州。

translations.literal: The next year he followed in attacking Han and took Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he joined the campaign against Han and captured Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 友諒走武昌，達追之。

translations.literal: Youliang fled to Wuchang; Da pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang fled to Wuchang, and Xu Da pursued him.

sentences.zh: 友諒出戰艦沔陽，達營漢陽沌口以遏之。

translations.literal: Youliang brought out warships at Mianyang; Da encamped at Hankou's Zhunkou to block him.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang brought his fleet out at Mianyang; Xu Da encamped at Zhunkou on the Han to block him.

sentences.zh: 進中書右丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，太祖定南昌，降將祝宗、康泰叛。

translations.literal: The next year the Founder secured Nanchang; the surrendered generals Zhu Zong and Kang Tai rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, after the Founder secured Nanchang, the surrendered generals Zhu Zong and Kang Tai rebelled.

sentences.zh: 達以沌口軍討平之。

translations.literal: Da with the Zhunkou army suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da marched from Zhunkou and put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 從援安豐，破吳將呂珍，遂圍廬州。

translations.literal: He followed in relieving Anfeng, defeated the Wu general Lü Zhen, and then besieged Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He helped relieve Anfeng, routed the Wu general Lü Zhen, and then laid siege to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 會漢人寇南昌，太祖召達自廬州來會師，遇於鄱陽湖。

translations.literal: It happened that Han men raided Nanchang; the Founder summoned Da from Luzhou to join forces; they met at Poyang Lake.
translations.idiomatic: When Han forces threatened Nanchang, the Founder recalled Xu Da from Luzhou; the armies met at Poyang Lake.

sentences.zh: 友諒軍甚盛，達身先諸將力戰，敗其前鋒，殺千五百人，獲一巨舟。

translations.literal: Youliang's army was very strong; Da with his person ahead of the generals fought fiercely, defeated their vanguard, killed fifteen hundred men, and captured one great ship.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang's army was overwhelming; Xu Da led the generals in a fierce assault, broke their vanguard, killed fifteen hundred men, and captured a great warship.

sentences.zh: 太祖知敵可破，而慮士誠內犯，即夜遣達還守應天，自帥諸將鏖戰，竟斃友諒。

translations.literal: The Founder knew the enemy could be broken but feared Shicheng would invade from within; that very night he sent Da back to garrison Yingtian, while he himself led the generals in bitter fighting and finally killed Youliang.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the enemy could be broken but fearing Zhang Shicheng might strike inland, the Founder that night sent Xu Da back to hold Yingtian and himself led the bitter fight that finally killed Youliang.

sentences.zh: 明年，太祖稱吳王，以達為左相國。

translations.literal: The next year the Founder styled himself King of Wu and made Da left prime minister.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Founder took the title King of Wu and made Xu Da his left prime minister.

sentences.zh: 復引兵圍廬州，克其城。

translations.literal: He again led troops to besiege Luzhou and captured its city.
translations.idiomatic: He again besieged Luzhou and took the city.

sentences.zh: 略下江陵、辰州、衡州、寶慶諸路，湖、湘平。

translations.literal: He overran and reduced Jiangling, Chenzhou, Hengzhou, Baoqing, and other circuits; Hunan and the Xiang region were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He overran Jiangling, Chen, Heng, Baoqing, and the other circuits until Hunan and the Xiang region were pacified.

sentences.zh: 召還，帥遇春等徇淮東，克泰州。

translations.literal: He was recalled and commanded Yuchun and others in marching through Huai-dong, capturing Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he led Chang Yuchun and others east along the Huai and took Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 吳人陷宜興，達還救復之。

translations.literal: Wu men seized Yixing; Da returned to rescue and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu forces seized Yixing, Xu Da marched back and recovered it.

sentences.zh: 復引兵渡江，克高郵，俘吳將士千餘人。

translations.literal: He again led troops across the river, captured Gaoyou, and took captive more than a thousand Wu officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river again, took Gaoyou, and captured more than a thousand Wu officers and men.

sentences.zh: 會遇春攻淮安，破吳軍于馬騾港，守將梅思祖以城降。

translations.literal: It happened that Yuchun attacked Huai'an, defeated Wu troops at Maluo Harbor, and the defending general Mei Sizu surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Chang Yuchun attacked Huai'an, routed the Wu army at Maluo Harbor, and the defender Mei Sizu surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 進破安豐，獲元將忻都，走左君弼，盡得其運艘。

translations.literal: Advancing he broke Anfeng, captured the Yuan general Xindu, drove off Zuo Junbi, and obtained all their transport ships.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on he broke Anfeng, captured the Yuan general Xindu, drove off Zuo Junbi, and seized all their transport ships.

sentences.zh: 元兵侵徐州，迎擊，大破之，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: Yuan troops invaded Xuzhou; he met and attacked them, utterly defeated them, and captured and beheaded men by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan forces invaded Xuzhou he met them head-on, routed them, and killed or captured tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 淮南、北悉平。

translations.literal: Huainan and the north were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan and the northern regions were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 師還，太祖議征吳。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Founder deliberated on campaigning against Wu.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, the Founder debated an expedition against Wu.

sentences.zh: 右相國李善長請緩之。

translations.literal: The right prime minister Li Shanchang requested to delay it.
translations.idiomatic: The right prime minister Li Shanchang urged delay.

sentences.zh: 達曰：「張氏汰而苛，大將李伯升輩徒擁子女玉帛，易與耳。

translations.literal: Da said: "The Zhang clan is dissolute and harsh; great generals like Li Bosheng and the rest merely hold wives, children, jade, and silks—they are easy to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da said, "The Zhang regime is decadent and harsh; commanders like Li Bosheng care only for wives, children, and treasure—they will be easy to overcome.

sentences.zh: 用事者，黃、蔡、葉三參軍，書生不知大計。

translations.literal: Those in power are the three staff officers Huang, Cai, and Ye—literati who do not know great strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power are the staff officers Huang, Cai, and Ye—scholars who know nothing of grand strategy.

sentences.zh: 臣奉主上威德，以大軍蹙之，三吳可計日定。」

translations.literal: Your subject, bearing the sovereign's majesty and virtue, with a great army pressing them, can fix the Three Wu regions within countable days.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty's servant leads the great army against them under your authority, the Three Wu can be settled within days.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅，拜達大將軍，平章遇春為副將軍，帥舟師二十萬人薄湖州。

translations.literal: The Founder was greatly pleased, appointed Da Grand General, made Pingzhang Yuchun vice general, and commanded a fleet of two hundred thousand men to press on Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was delighted, made Xu Da grand general and Chang Yuchun his deputy, and sent two hundred thousand men by water against Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 敵三道出戰，達亦分三軍應之，別遣兵扼其歸路。

translations.literal: The enemy came out to fight on three roads; Da also divided three armies to meet them and separately sent troops to block their route of return.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy advanced on three fronts; Xu Da met them with three divisions and sent another force to cut off their retreat.

sentences.zh: 敵戰敗返走，不得入城。

translations.literal: The enemy were defeated in battle and turned back in flight, unable to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, the enemy fled but could not re-enter the city.

sentences.zh: 還戰，大破之，擒將吏二百人，圍其城。

translations.literal: They fought again; he utterly defeated them, captured two hundred officers and clerks, and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: When they turned to fight again he routed them, took two hundred officers and officials prisoner, and invested the city.

sentences.zh: 士誠遣呂珍等以兵六萬赴救，屯舊館，築五寨自固。

translations.literal: Shicheng sent Lü Zhen and others with sixty thousand troops to the rescue; they encamped at Jiuguan and built five stockades to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng sent Lü Zhen and others with sixty thousand men; they camped at Jiuguan and built five fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 達使遇春等為十壘以遮之。

translations.literal: Da had Yuchun and others build ten ramparts to block them.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da had Chang Yuchun and others erect ten camps to block them.

sentences.zh: 士誠自以精兵來援，大破之于皁林。

translations.literal: Shicheng himself came with crack troops to the rescue; he utterly defeated them at Zaolin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng came in person with elite troops; Xu Da routed them at Zaolin.

sentences.zh: 士誠走，遂拔升山水陸寨。

translations.literal: Shicheng fled; he then captured the Shengshan land and water stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng fled, and Xu Da then took the Shengshan camps by land and water.

sentences.zh: 五太子、硃暹、呂珍等皆降，以徇於城下，湖州降。

translations.literal: The Fifth Prince, Zhu Xian, Lü Zhen, and others all surrendered; he paraded them below the city, and Huzhou surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Fifth Prince, Zhu Xian, Lü Zhen, and the rest surrendered; paraded before the walls, they brought about Huzhou's surrender.

sentences.zh: 遂下吳江州，從太湖進圍平江。

translations.literal: He then reduced Wujiang Prefecture and advanced from Lake Tai to besiege Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Wujiang and advanced from Lake Tai to besiege Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 達軍葑門，遇春軍虎丘，郭子興軍婁門，華雲龍軍胥門，湯和軍閶門，王弼軍盤門，張溫軍西門，康茂才軍北門，耿炳文軍城東北，仇成軍城西南，何文輝軍城西北，築長圍困之。

translations.literal: Da's army at the Fumeng Gate, Yuchun's at Tiger Hill, Guo Zixing's at the Lou Gate, Hua Yunlong's at the Xu Gate, Tang He's at the Chang Gate, Wang Bi's at the Pan Gate, Zhang Wen's at the West Gate, Kang Maocai's at the North Gate, Geng Bingwen's northeast of the city, Qiu Cheng's southwest, He Wenhui's northwest—they built a long encirclement to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da held the Fumeng Gate, Chang Yuchun Tiger Hill, Guo Zixing the Lou Gate, Hua Yunlong the Xu Gate, Tang He the Chang Gate, Wang Bi the Pan Gate, Zhang Wen the West Gate, Kang Maocai the North Gate, Geng Bingwen the northeast, Qiu Cheng the southwest, and He Wenhui the northwest, forming a long encirclement around the city.

sentences.zh: 架木塔與城中浮屠等。

translations.literal: They erected wooden towers equal to the pagodas within the city.
translations.idiomatic: They built wooden towers as tall as the city's pagodas.

sentences.zh: 別築台三成，瞰城中，置弓弩火筒。

translations.literal: Separately they built platforms in three tiers, overlooking the city, and set up crossbows, fire-lances, and tubes.
translations.idiomatic: They raised three-tiered platforms overlooking the walls and mounted crossbows and fire-lances.

sentences.zh: 臺上又置巨礮，所擊輒糜碎。

translations.literal: On the platforms they further set great bombards; whatever they struck was instantly pulverized.
translations.idiomatic: Great bombards on the platforms shattered whatever they struck.

sentences.zh: 城中大震。

translations.literal: Within the city there was great shock.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through the city.

sentences.zh: 達遣使請事，太祖敕勞之曰：「將軍謀勇絕倫，故能遏亂略，削群雄。

translations.literal: Da sent an envoy to request instructions; the Founder issued an edict to comfort him, saying: "The general's stratagem and courage are unmatched, and therefore he can check rebellion and overrun, and cut down the many strong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da sent to ask for orders; the Founder wrote to praise him: "Your stratagem and courage are unmatched; that is how you check rebellion and cut down rival powers.

sentences.zh: 今事必稟命，此將軍之忠，吾甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Now on every matter you must report for orders—this is the general's loyalty, which I greatly commend.
translations.idiomatic: That you report on every move shows your loyalty, and I commend it highly.

sentences.zh: 然將在外，君不禦。

translations.literal: Yet when the general is abroad, the ruler does not direct him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the general is in the field, the ruler does not micromanage him.

sentences.zh: 軍中緩急，將軍其便宜行之，吾不中制。」

translations.literal: In the army, whether urgent or slack, the general should as convenient carry things out; I will not interfere from the center.
translations.idiomatic: In matters urgent or routine, act as you see fit—I will not second-guess you from the capital.

sentences.zh: 既而平江破，執士誠，傳送應天，得勝兵二十五萬人。

translations.literal: Soon after Pingjiang was broken, they seized Shicheng and sent him under escort to Yingtian, obtaining twenty-five thousand victorious troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Pingjiang fell; Zhang Shicheng was seized and sent to Yingtian, and twenty-five thousand seasoned troops were taken.

sentences.zh: 城之將破也，達與遇春約曰：「師入，我營其左，公營其右。」

translations.literal: When the city was about to be broken, Da and Yuchun agreed, saying: "When the army enters, I shall encamp on its left, and you on its right.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall, Xu Da and Chang Yuchun agreed: "When the army enters, I will take the left and you the right.

sentences.zh: 又令荅士曰：「掠民財者死，毀民居者死，離營二十里者死。」

translations.literal: He further ordered the answer to the troops, saying: "Whoever plunders the people's wealth dies; whoever destroys the people's dwellings dies; whoever leaves camp twenty li dies."
translations.idiomatic: He also proclaimed to the troops: "Anyone who loots civilians, destroys homes, or strays twenty li from camp will be put to death."

sentences.zh: 既入，吳人安堵如故。

translations.literal: After they entered, the Wu people were settled in their places as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the entry the people of Wu lived undisturbed as before.

sentences.zh: 師還，封信國公。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was enfeoffed as Duke of the State.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was enfeoffed as Duke of the State.

sentences.zh: 尋拜征虜大將軍，以遇春為副，帥步騎二十五萬人，北取中原，太祖親祃于龍江。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians, with Yuchun as deputy, commanding two hundred fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to seize the Central Plains in the north; the Founder personally performed the libation at Longjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General Who Subdues the Barbarians, with Chang Yuchun as his deputy, and led two hundred fifty thousand foot and horse north to take the Central Plains; the Founder personally performed the libation at Longjiang.

sentences.zh: 是時稱名將，必推達、遇春。

translations.literal: At that time in naming great generals, one invariably ranked Da and Yuchun first.
translations.idiomatic: At that time any roll of great generals began with Xu Da and Chang Yuchun.

sentences.zh: 兩人才勇相類，皆太祖所倚重。

translations.literal: The two men's talent and courage were alike; both were what the Founder relied on heavily.
translations.idiomatic: The two were matched in talent and courage, and both were pillars of the Founder's power.

sentences.zh: 遇春剽疾敢深入，而達尤長於謀略。

translations.literal: Yuchun was swift and daring in deep penetration, while Da was especially skilled in stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun was swift and daring in deep strikes, while Xu Da excelled above all in strategy.

sentences.zh: 遇春下城邑不能無誅僇，達所至不擾，即獲壯士與諜，結以恩義，俾為己用。

translations.literal: When Yuchun reduced cities and towns he could not be without executions and punishments; wherever Da arrived he did not disturb, and when he obtained stalwart men and spies he bound them with favor and righteousness and made them serve his use.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun could hardly take a city without executions; wherever Xu Da went the people were undisturbed, and stalwarts and spies he won over with kindness he put to his own use.

sentences.zh: 由此多樂附大將軍者。

translations.literal: From this many were glad to attach themselves to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason many were glad to serve under the Grand General.

sentences.zh: 至是，太祖諭諸將禦軍持重有紀律，戰勝攻取得為將之體者，莫如大將軍達。

translations.literal: By now the Founder instructed the generals that in governing the army, holding weight and having discipline, and in defeating the enemy and attacking to gain—the substance of being a general—none matched Grand General Da.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Founder told his generals that in holding an army with discipline and gravity, and in the art of victory and conquest, none matched Grand General Xu Da.

sentences.zh: 又謂達，進取方略，宜自山東始。

translations.literal: He also told Da that the strategy of advance should begin from Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Xu Da that the advance should begin in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 師行，克沂州，降守將王宣。

translations.literal: The army marched; he captured Yizhou and the defending general Wang Xuan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On the march he took Yizhou and the defender Wang Xuan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進克嶧州，王宣復叛，擊斬之。

translations.literal: Advancing he captured Yizhou [Yi prefecture]; Wang Xuan rebelled again; he attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and took Yi Prefecture; when Wang Xuan rebelled again, Xu Da struck and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 莒、密、海諸州悉下。

translations.literal: Ju, Mi, Hai, and the other prefectures were all reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Ju, Mi, Hai, and the other prefectures all fell.

sentences.zh: 乃使韓政分兵扼河，張興祖取東平、濟寧，而自帥大軍拔益都，徇下濰、膠諸州縣。

translations.literal: He then had Han Zheng divide troops to hold the river, Zhang Xingzu take Dongping and Jining, while he himself commanded the great army to seize Yidu and march through reducing Wei, Jiao, and the other prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Han Zheng to hold the river line, Zhang Xingzu to take Dongping and Jining, and himself led the main force to seize Yidu and sweep through Wei, Jiao, and the other counties.

sentences.zh: 濟南降，分兵取登、萊。

translations.literal: Jinan surrendered; he divided troops to take Deng and Lai.
translations.idiomatic: Jinan surrendered, and he sent detachments to take Deng and Lai.

sentences.zh: 齊地悉定。

translations.literal: The Qi region was entirely settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi region was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，太祖幸汴梁，召達詣行在所，置酒勞之，且謀北伐。

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, the Founder visited Bianliang, summoned Da to the mobile court, set out wine to comfort him, and also deliberated on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, the Founder went to Bianliang, summoned Xu Da to his camp, feasted him, and planned the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 達曰：「大軍平齊魯，掃河洛，王保保逡巡觀望；

translations.literal: Da said: "The great army has pacified Qi and Lu and swept He and Luo; Wang Baobao hesitates and watches from afar;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da said, "The great army has pacified Qi and Lu and swept the He and Luo regions; Wang Baobao hangs back and watches;

sentences.zh: 潼關既克，思齊輩狼狽西奔。

translations.literal: Tong Pass having been captured, Siji and his ilk fled west in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Pass is taken and men like Siji have fled west in disorder;

sentences.zh: 元聲援已絕，今乘勢直搗元都，可不戰有也。」

translations.literal: Yuan reinforcements are already cut off; now, riding the momentum to strike straight at the Yuan capital, one can have it without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan reinforcements are cut off—if we strike straight at Dadu now, we can take it without a battle.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 達復進曰：「元都克，而其主北走，將窮追之乎？」

translations.literal: Da again advanced and said: "When the Yuan capital is captured and its ruler flees north, will you pursue him to the end?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da went on, "When Dadu falls and the Yuan ruler flees north, will you pursue him to the end?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「元運衰矣，行自澌滅，不煩窮兵。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Yuan fortune is already declining; it will in time dissolve of itself—no need to trouble with extreme military force.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The Yuan mandate is spent—it will collapse on its own. There is no need for endless pursuit.

sentences.zh: 出塞之後，固守封疆，防其侵軼可也。」

translations.literal: After he goes beyond the passes, firmly guard the borders and frontiers and guard against their raids and incursions—that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Once he has fled beyond the frontier, hold the borders firm and guard against raids—that will be enough."

sentences.zh: 達頓首受命。

translations.literal: Da bowed his head to the ground and received the command.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da kowtowed and accepted the orders.

sentences.zh: 遂與副將軍會師河陰，遣裨將分道徇河北地，連下衛輝、彰德、廣平。

translations.literal: He then joined the vice general at Heyin, sent lieutenant generals on separate roads to march through Hebei territory, and in succession reduced Weihui, Zhangde, and Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the deputy commander at Heyin, sent lieutenants along separate routes through Hebei, and in succession took Weihui, Zhangde, and Guangping.

sentences.zh: 師次臨清，使傅友德開陸道通步騎，顧時浚河通舟師，遂引而北。

translations.literal: The army halted at Linqing; he had Fu Youde open a land route for infantry and cavalry, Gu Shi dredged the river for the fleet, and then led them north.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Linqing; Fu Youde opened a land route for the infantry and cavalry, Gu Shi dredged the river for the fleet, and the force marched north.

sentences.zh: 遇春已克德州，合兵取長蘆，扼直沽，作浮橋以濟師。

translations.literal: Yuchun had already captured Dezhou; they united forces to take Changlu, held Zhigu, and built a pontoon bridge to ferry the army.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun had already taken Dezhou; the armies united to seize Changlu, held Zhigu, and built a pontoon bridge to cross.

sentences.zh: 水陸並進，大敗元軍於河西務，進克通州。

translations.literal: By land and water they advanced together, utterly defeated Yuan troops at Hexiwu, and advanced to capture Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing by land and water together, they routed the Yuan army at Hexiwu and took Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 順帝帥後妃太子北去。

translations.literal: Emperor Shundi led the empresses, consorts, and crown prince north in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shundi fled north with his consorts and the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 逾日，達陳兵齊化門，填濠登城。

translations.literal: The next day Da arrayed troops at the Qihua Gate, filled the moat, and ascended the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xu Da drew up his troops at the Qihua Gate, filled the moat, and scaled the walls.

sentences.zh: 監國淮王帖木兒不花，左丞相慶童，平章迭兒必失、樸賽因不花，右丞張康伯，御史中丞滿川等不降，斬之，其餘不戮一人。

translations.literal: The regent Prince Huai Timur Buqa, left chancellor Qing Tong, pingzhang Dierbish, Pusaiyin Buqa, right chancellor Zhang Kangbo, censor-in-chief Manchuan, and others would not surrender and were beheaded; of the rest not one was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The regent Prince Huai Timur Buqa, the left chancellor Qing Tong, the pingzhang Dierbish and Pusaiyin Buqa, the right chancellor Zhang Kangbo, the censor-in-chief Manchuan, and others who refused to surrender were beheaded; not another soul was killed.

sentences.zh: 封府庫，籍圖書寶物，令指揮張勝以兵千人守宮殿門，使宦者護視諸宮人、妃、主，禁士卒毋所侵暴。

translations.literal: He sealed the treasuries, registered books, maps, and treasures, ordered Commander Zhang Sheng with a thousand troops to guard the palace gates, had eunuchs protect and watch over the palace women, consorts, and princesses, and forbade the soldiers any violation or outrage.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the treasuries and inventoried books and treasures, posted Commander Zhang Sheng with a thousand men at the palace gates, set eunuchs to guard the palace women and princesses, and forbade the troops any violence.

sentences.zh: 吏民安居，市不易肆。

translations.literal: Officials and people dwelt in peace; the markets did not change their stalls.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners lived undisturbed, and the markets carried on as before.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔以元都為北平府，置六衛，留孫興祖等守之，而命達與遇春進取山西。

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, an edict made the Yuan capital Beiping Prefecture, established six guards, left Sun Xingzu and others to garrison it, and ordered Da and Yuchun to advance and seize Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, an edict renamed the Yuan capital Beiping Prefecture, established six guards, left Sun Xingzu and others to hold it, and ordered Xu Da and Chang Yuchun to take Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 遇春先下保定、中山、真定，馮勝、湯和下懷慶，度太行，取澤、潞，達以大軍繼之。

translations.literal: Yuchun first reduced Baoding, Zhongshan, and Zhending; Feng Sheng and Tang He reduced Huaiqing, crossed the Taihang range, and took Ze and Lu; Da followed with the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun first took Baoding, Zhongshan, and Zhending; Feng Sheng and Tang He took Huaiqing, crossed the Taihang, and seized Ze and Lu; Xu Da followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 時擴廓帖木兒方引兵出雁門，將由居庸以攻北平。

translations.literal: At that time Köke Temür was just leading troops out through Yanmen, intending to attack Beiping by way of Juyong.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür was then marching out through Yanmen Pass, intending to strike Beiping via Juyong.

sentences.zh: 達聞之，與諸將謀曰：「擴廓遠出，太原必虛。

translations.literal: When Da heard this, he deliberated with the generals, saying: "Köke Temür has marched far away; Taiyuan must be empty.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Xu Da consulted the generals: "Köke Temür is far afield—Taiyuan must be undefended.

sentences.zh: 北平有孫都督在，足以禦之。

translations.literal: Beiping has Commander Sun there; that is sufficient to defend against him.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Sun at Beiping can hold him off.

sentences.zh: 今乘敵不備，直搗太原，使進不得戰，退無所守，所謂批亢搗虛者也。

translations.literal: Now, riding the enemy's lack of preparation, strike straight at Taiyuan, so that advancing they cannot fight and retreating they have nowhere to hold—this is what is called striking the throat and raiding the empty place.
translations.idiomatic: If we strike Taiyuan now while they are unprepared, they cannot advance to fight and have nowhere to retreat—that is to strike the vitals and raid the undefended point.

sentences.zh: 彼若西還自救，此成擒耳。」

translations.literal: If they return west to save themselves, this one will be captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: If they turn west to save themselves, we will take them alive.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The generals all said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The generals all agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃引兵趨太原。

translations.literal: He then led troops in haste toward Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: They marched at once on Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 擴廓至保安，果還救。

translations.literal: Köke Temür reached Bao'an and indeed returned to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür reached Bao'an and turned back as expected.

sentences.zh: 達選精兵夜襲其營。

translations.literal: Da selected crack troops and by night raided his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da chose elite troops and raided his camp by night.

sentences.zh: 擴廓以十八騎遁去。

translations.literal: Köke Temür fled with eighteen horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür escaped with eighteen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 盡降其眾，遂克太原。

translations.literal: All his host surrendered; he then captured Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His entire force surrendered, and Xu Da took Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 乘勢收大同，分兵徇未下州縣。

translations.literal: Riding the momentum he recovered Datong and divided troops to march through prefectures and counties not yet reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the advantage he took Datong and sent detachments to reduce the remaining counties.

sentences.zh: 山西悉平。

translations.literal: Shanxi was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 二年引兵西渡河。

translations.literal: In the second year he led troops west across the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he led his army west across the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 至鹿台，張思道遁，遂克奉元。

translations.literal: Reaching Lutai, Zhang Sidao fled, and he then captured Fengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At Lutai, Zhang Sidao fled, and he took Fengyuan.

sentences.zh: 時遇春下鳳翔，李思齊走臨洮，達會諸將議所向。

translations.literal: At that time Yuchun had reduced Fengxiang; Li Siqi fled to Lintao; Da gathered the generals to deliberate on where to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun had taken Fengxiang; Li Siqi fled to Lintao; Xu Da convened the generals to decide their next move.

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「張思道之才不如李思齊，而慶陽易於臨洮，請先慶陽。」

translations.literal: All said: "Zhang Sidao's talent is not equal to Li Siqi's, and Qingyang is easier than Lintao—we request to take Qingyang first.
translations.idiomatic: All urged taking Qingyang first: Zhang Sidao was the lesser foe, and Qingyang would be easier than Lintao.

sentences.zh: 達曰：「不然，慶陽城險而兵精，猝未易拔也。

translations.literal: Da said: "Not so—Qingyang's walls are perilous and its troops crack; suddenly it is not easy to pull out.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da said, "No—Qingyang is strongly fortified and well garrisoned; it cannot be taken quickly.

sentences.zh: 臨洮北界河、湟，西控羌、戎，得之，其人足備戰鬥，物產足佐軍儲。

translations.literal: Lintao on the north borders the He and Huang rivers; on the west it controls the Qiang and Rong—obtaining it, its people suffice to supply fighting, its products suffice to aid army stores.
translations.idiomatic: Lintao borders the He and Huang rivers on the north and commands the Qiang and Rong on the west; its people would supply fighting men and its produce would fill the army's stores.

sentences.zh: 蹙以大兵，思齊不走，則束手縛矣。

translations.literal: Pressing him with a great army, if Siqi does not flee, then he will be bound with hands tied.
translations.idiomatic: If we press Li Siqi with the main army, he will either flee or be taken bound.

sentences.zh: 臨洮既克，于旁郡何有？」

translations.literal: Once Lintao is captured, what of the neighboring prefectures?"
translations.idiomatic: Once Lintao falls, what will the neighboring prefectures matter?"

sentences.zh: 遂渡隴，克秦州，下伏羌、寧遠，入鞏昌，遣右副將軍馮勝逼臨洮，思齊果不戰降。

translations.literal: He then crossed Long, captured Qinzhou, reduced Fuqiang and Ningyuan, entered Gongchang, sent the right vice general Feng Sheng to press Lintao, and Siqi indeed surrendered without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed Long, took Qinzhou, reduced Fuqiang and Ningyuan, entered Gongchang, and sent the right deputy Feng Sheng against Lintao; Li Siqi surrendered without a fight.

sentences.zh: 分兵克蘭州，襲走豫王，盡收其部落輜重。

translations.literal: He divided troops to capture Lanzhou, raided and drove off the Prince of Yu, and entirely seized his tribal baggage and heavy equipment.
translations.idiomatic: A detachment took Lanzhou, routed the Prince of Yu, and seized all his tribal baggage.

sentences.zh: 還出蕭關，下平涼。

translations.literal: Returning he came out through Xiaoguan and reduced Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He returned through Xiaoguan and took Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 思道走寧夏，為擴廓所執，其弟良臣以慶陽降。

translations.literal: Sidao fled to Ningxia and was seized by Köke Temür; his younger brother Liangchen surrendered Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sidao fled to Ningxia and was seized by Köke Temür; his brother Liangchen surrendered Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 達遣薛顯受之。

translations.literal: Da sent Xue Xian to receive the surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da sent Xue Xian to accept the surrender.

sentences.zh: 良臣復叛，夜出兵襲傷顯。

translations.literal: Liangchen rebelled again; by night he sent troops in a surprise attack and wounded Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen rebelled again and by night attacked and wounded Xue Xian.

sentences.zh: 達督軍圍之。

translations.literal: Da supervised the army in besieging it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da personally directed the siege.

sentences.zh: 擴廓遣將來援，逆擊敗去，遂拔慶陽。

translations.literal: Köke Temür sent generals to come to the rescue; he met and attacked them and drove them off, then captured Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür sent relief forces; Xu Da met and routed them and took Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 良臣父子投于井，引出斬之。

translations.literal: Liangchen father and son threw themselves into a well; they were drawn out and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen and his son threw themselves into a well; they were hauled out and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 盡定陝西地。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi region was entirely settled.
translations.idiomatic: All of Shaanxi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔達班師，賜白金文綺甚厚。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Da to withdraw the army and bestowed white gold and patterned silks in great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled Xu Da and rewarded him lavishly with silver and brocade.

sentences.zh: 將論功大封，會擴廓攻蘭州，殺指揮使，副將軍遇春已卒，三年春帝復以達為大將軍，平章李文忠為副將軍，分道出兵。

translations.literal: They were about to deliberate on merit and grant great enfeoffments when it happened that Köke Temür attacked Lanzhou and killed the commander; the vice general Yuchun had already died; in the spring of the third year the Emperor again made Da grand general and Pingzhang Li Wenzhong vice general, and they marched out on separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Merit awards were pending when Köke Temür attacked Lanzhou and killed its commander; Chang Yuchun had died; in the spring of the third year the Emperor again made Xu Da grand general and Li Wenzhong his deputy, and they marched on separate routes.

sentences.zh: 達自潼關出西道，搗定西，取擴廓。

translations.literal: Da from Tong Pass marched out on the western route, struck Dingxi, and took Köke Temür.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da marched west from Tong Pass toward Dingxi to take Köke Temür.

sentences.zh: 文忠自居庸出東道，絕大漠，追元嗣主。

translations.literal: Wenzhong from Juyong marched out on the eastern route, crossed the great desert, and pursued the Yuan heir.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenzhong marched east from Juyong, crossed the great desert, and pursued the Yuan heir.

sentences.zh: 達至定西，擴廓退屯沈兒峪，進軍薄之。

translations.literal: Da reached Dingxi; Köke Temür withdrew and encamped at Shen'er Ravine; the advancing army pressed close.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da reached Dingxi; Köke Temür fell back to Shen'er Ravine; the Ming army closed in.

sentences.zh: 隔溝而壘，日數交。

translations.literal: Separated by a ravine they built ramparts; daily they clashed several times.
translations.idiomatic: The two sides fortified camps on opposite sides of a ravine and skirmished daily.

sentences.zh: 擴廓遣精兵從間道劫東南壘，左丞胡德濟倉卒失措，軍驚擾，達帥兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: Köke Temür sent crack troops by a bypath to raid the southeast rampart; left chancellor Hu Deji was suddenly at a loss and the army was alarmed and disturbed; Da led troops and struck them back.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür sent elite troops by a hidden path to storm the southeast camp; the left chancellor Hu Deji panicked and the army wavered; Xu Da led a counterattack and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 德濟，大海子也，達以其功臣子，械送之京師，而斬其下指揮等數人以徇。

translations.literal: Deji was Dahai's son; Da, because he was a meritorious minister's son, sent him in fetters to the capital, but beheaded several of his subordinate commanders and others as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Deji was the son of the meritorious minister Dahai; Xu Da sent him in chains to the capital but beheaded several of his subordinate commanders as an example.

sentences.zh: 明日，整兵奪溝，殊死戰，大破擴廓兵。

translations.literal: The next day he arrayed the army, seized the ravine, fought a death struggle, and utterly defeated Köke Temür's troops.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he reformed the ranks, seized the ravine in a desperate fight, and routed Köke Temür's army.

sentences.zh: 擒郯王、文濟王及國公、平章以下文武僚屬千八百六十餘人，將士八萬四千五百余人，馬駝雜畜以巨萬計。

translations.literal: He captured the Prince of Tan, the Prince of Wenji, and more than 1,860 civil and military subordinates from state dukes and pingzhang downward, more than 84,500 officers and soldiers, and horses, camels, and miscellaneous livestock by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the Princes of Tan and Wenji and more than 1,860 civil and military officials down to state dukes and pingzhang, 84,500 officers and men, and tens of thousands of horses, camels, and livestock.

sentences.zh: 擴廓僅挾妻子數人奔和林。

translations.literal: Köke Temür fled to Karakorum with only a few wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür escaped to Karakorum with only a few wives and children.

sentences.zh: 德濟至京，帝釋之，而以書諭達：「將軍效衛青不斬蘇建耳，獨不見穰苴之待莊賈乎？

translations.literal: Deji reached the capital; the Emperor released him and with a letter instructed Da: "The general imitates Wei Qing in not beheading Su Jian—but has he alone not seen how Rangju treated Zhuang Jia?
translations.idiomatic: Hu Deji reached the capital and was released; the Emperor wrote to Xu Da: "You imitate Wei Qing, who spared Su Jian—but have you forgotten how Rangju dealt with Zhuang Jia?

sentences.zh: 將軍誅之，則已。

translations.literal: If the general had executed him, that would have been that.
translations.idiomatic: If you had executed him, that would have been the end of it.

sentences.zh: 今下廷議，吾且念其信州、諸暨功，不忍加誅。

translations.literal: Now it goes down to court deliberation; I for the moment recall his merit at Xinzhou and Zhuji and cannot bear to add execution.
translations.idiomatic: Now the matter goes to court—but I recall his service at Xinzhou and Zhuji and will not have him put to death.

sentences.zh: 繼自今，將軍毋事姑息。」

translations.literal: From now on, general, do not be lenient in such matters.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter, General, do not be so lenient.

sentences.zh: 達既破擴廓，即帥師自徽州南一百八渡至略陽，克沔州，入連雲棧，攻興元，取之。

translations.literal: Da, having defeated Köke Temür, then commanded the army from Huizhou south through the One Hundred Eight Fords to Lueyang, captured Mianzhou, entered the Linked Cloud Plank Road, attacked Xingyuan, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Köke Temür, Xu Da led his army south from Huizhou through the One Hundred Eight Fords to Lueyang, took Mianzhou, entered the Linked Cloud Plank Road, and captured Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 而副將軍文忠亦克應昌，獲元嫡孫妃主將相。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the vice general Wenzhong also captured Yingchang and obtained the Yuan heir's consorts, princesses, and chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Li Wenzhong took Yingchang and captured the Yuan heir's consorts, princesses, and chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 先後露布聞，詔振旅還京師。

translations.literal: Successively victory bulletins arrived; an edict ordered the army to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Victory reports arrived in succession; an edict ordered the armies home to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝迎勞于龍江。

translations.literal: The Emperor went out to welcome and comfort them at Longjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor went out to welcome them at Longjiang.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔大封功臣，授達開國輔運推誠宣力武臣，特進光祿大夫、左柱國、太傅、中書右丞相參軍國事，改封魏國公，歲祿五千石，予世券。

translations.literal: He then issued an edict for great enfeoffment of meritorious ministers, appointing Da as Martial Minister Who Founded the State, Aided the Fortune, Pushed Forward Sincerity, and Proclaimed Merit; specially promoted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Left Pillar of the State, Grand Tutor, and Right Chancellor of the Secretariat participating in state affairs; changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Wei; annual stipend five thousand piculs; granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then enfeoffed the great ministers: Xu Da was made founding martial minister who aided the dynasty with sincere merit, specially promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Left Pillar of the State, Grand Tutor, and right chancellor of the Secretariat with a voice in state affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Wei with an annual stipend of five thousand piculs and a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 明年帥盛熙等赴北平練軍馬，修城池，徙山后軍民實諸衛府，置二百五十四屯，墾田一千三百餘頃。

translations.literal: The next year he led Sheng Xi and others to Beiping to drill troops and horses, repair walls and moats, relocate mountain-behind military and civilians to fill the various guard prefectures, established 254 colonies, and opened more than 1,300 qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he led Sheng Xi and others to Beiping to drill troops, repair the walls, resettle frontier populations into the guard districts, established 254 military colonies, and opened more than 1,300 qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 其冬，召還。

translations.literal: That winter he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 五年復大發兵征擴廓。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again raised a great army to campaign against Köke Temür.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year a great army was again raised against Köke Temür.

sentences.zh: 達以征虜大將軍出中道，左副將軍李文忠出東道，征西將軍馮勝出西道，各將五萬騎出塞。

translations.literal: Da as General Who Subdues the Barbarians marched out on the central route; left vice general Li Wenzhong on the eastern route; General Who Subdues the West Feng Sheng on the western route—each leading fifty thousand cavalry beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da marched as General Who Subdues the Barbarians on the central route, Li Wenzhong on the east, and Feng Sheng on the west—each with fifty thousand horse beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 達遣都督藍玉擊敗擴廓於土刺河。

translations.literal: Da sent Commissioner-in-Chief Lan Yu to defeat Köke Temür at the Tula River.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da sent Commissioner Lan Yu to defeat Köke Temür on the Tula River.

sentences.zh: 擴廓與賀宗哲合兵力拒，達戰不利，死者數萬人。

translations.literal: Köke Temür united forces with He Zongzhe to resist; Da's battle went ill and tens of thousands died.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür joined He Zongzhe to resist; Xu Da was defeated and tens of thousands were killed.

sentences.zh: 帝以達功大，弗問也。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Da's merit was great, did not inquire into it.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Xu Da's great merit, the Emperor did not hold him to account.

sentences.zh: 時文忠軍亦不利，引還。

translations.literal: At that time Wenzhong's army also fared ill and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenzhong's army had also fared badly and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 獨勝至西涼獲全勝，坐匿駝馬，賞不行，事具《文忠》、《勝傳》。

translations.literal: Only Sheng reached Xiliang and obtained complete victory, but sat on concealed camels and horses and his reward was not carried out—the matter is fully set forth in the Wenzhong and Sheng biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Only Feng Sheng reached Xiliang victorious, but concealed camels and horses from the spoils and received no reward—the full accounts are in the biographies of Li Wenzhong and Feng Sheng.

sentences.zh: 明年，達復帥諸將行邊，破敵於答剌海，還軍北平，留三年而歸。

translations.literal: The next year Da again commanded the generals on border patrol, defeated the enemy at Dalai Sea, returned the army to Beiping, remained three years, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Xu Da again patrolled the frontier, defeated the enemy at Dalai Sea, returned to Beiping, stayed three years, and came home.

sentences.zh: 十四年，復帥湯和等討乃兒不花。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he again commanded Tang He and others to campaign against Nayirbuqa.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he again led Tang He and others against Nayirbuqa.

sentences.zh: 已，復還鎮。

translations.literal: When done, he again returned to garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: When that was done he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 每歲春出，冬暮召還，以為常。

translations.literal: Every year he marched out in spring and was recalled in late winter—this was the constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he marched out in spring and was recalled in late winter—a fixed routine.

sentences.zh: 還輒上將印，賜休沐，宴見歡飲，有布衣兄弟稱，而達愈恭慎。

translations.literal: On returning he invariably surrendered the general's seal, was granted rest and bathing, received banquets and audiences with joyful drinking, and was addressed as a brother in plain cloth—but Da became ever more respectful and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: On each return he surrendered his seal, was granted leave, and was feasted as an old comrade in plain cloth—but Xu Da grew only more respectful and cautious.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗從容言：「徐兄功大，未有甯居，可賜以舊邸。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once said at ease: "Elder Brother Xu's merit is great and he has no settled dwelling; the old residence may be bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once said casually, "Brother Xu's merit is great and he has no settled home—I should give him my old residence.

sentences.zh: 舊邸者，太祖為吳王時所居也。

translations.literal: The old residence was where the Founder had dwelt when he was King of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: That residence was where the Founder had lived as King of Wu.

sentences.zh: 達固辭。

translations.literal: Da firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝與達之邸，強飲之醉，而蒙之被，舁臥正寢。

translations.literal: One day the Emperor went to Da's residence, forced him to drink until drunk, covered him with a quilt, and had him carried to lie in the main chamber.
translations.idiomatic: One day the Emperor visited Xu Da's house, made him drink until drunk, covered him with a quilt, and had him carried to the main chamber.

sentences.zh: 達醒，驚趨下階，俯伏呼死罪。

translations.literal: When Da awoke, startled he hurried down the steps, prostrated himself, and cried out his capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Da awoke he rushed down the steps in alarm, prostrated himself, and cried that he deserved death.

sentences.zh: 帝覘之，大悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor peeped at him and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor watched and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 乃命有司即舊邸前治甲第，表其坊曰「大功」。

translations.literal: He then ordered the authorities to build a fine mansion before the old residence and inscribed its ward as "Great Merit."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a grand mansion built before the old residence and named the ward "Great Merit."

sentences.zh: 胡惟庸為丞相，欲結好于達，達薄其人，不答，則賂達閽者福壽使圖達。

translations.literal: Hu Weiyong as chancellor wished to form friendly ties with Da; Da looked down on the man and did not respond; he then bribed Da's gatekeeper Fushou to spy on and plot against Da.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Weiyong was chancellor he sought Xu Da's friendship; Xu Da despised him and refused; Hu then bribed Xu Da's gatekeeper Fushou to spy on him.

sentences.zh: 福壽發之，達亦不問；

translations.literal: Fushou exposed it; Da also did not inquire;
translations.idiomatic: Fushou exposed the plot; Xu Da did not pursue it;

sentences.zh: 惟時時為帝言惟庸不任相。

translations.literal: only from time to time told the Emperor that Weiyong was unfit to serve as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: but told the Emperor again and again that Hu Weiyong was unfit to be chancellor.

sentences.zh: 後果敗，帝益重達。

translations.literal: Later he indeed was ruined; the Emperor valued Da all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu was ruined at last, the Emperor valued Xu Da all the more.

sentences.zh: 十七年，太陰犯上將，帝心惡之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the moon eclipsed the General Star; the Emperor's heart was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year a lunar eclipse struck the General Star, and the Emperor was troubled.

sentences.zh: 達在北平病背疽，稍愈，帝遣達長子輝祖齎敕往勞，尋召還。

translations.literal: Da at Beiping was ill with a back carbuncle; when slightly recovered, the Emperor sent Da's eldest son Huizu bearing an edict to comfort him, then soon recalled him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da fell ill with a back carbuncle at Beiping; when he improved slightly the Emperor sent his eldest son Huizu with an edict of condolence, then recalled him.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，病篤，遂卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: The next year in the second month his illness was critical; he then died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the second month, his illness turned critical and he died at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 帝為輟朝，臨喪悲慟不已。

translations.literal: The Emperor for his sake suspended court and at the funeral grieved and sobbed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor suspended court and mourned at the funeral without cease.

sentences.zh: 追封中山王，諡武寧，贈三世皆王爵。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongshan, posthumous name Wuning, with three generations of forebears all granted princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongshan with the posthumous name Wuning, and three generations of ancestors were given princely rank.

sentences.zh: 賜葬鐘山之陰，禦制神道碑文。

translations.literal: Bestowed burial on the north slope of Bell Mountain; the Emperor himself composed the spirit-way stele inscription.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried on the north slope of Bell Mountain, with an imperial inscription for the spirit-way stele.

sentences.zh: 配享太廟，肖像功臣廟，位皆第一。

translations.literal: He received paired sacrifice in the Grand Temple; his portrait in the Meritorious Ministers Temple—both places first in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was given paired sacrifice in the Grand Temple and the foremost place in the Meritorious Ministers Temple.

sentences.zh: 達言簡慮精。

translations.literal: Da's words were concise and his deliberations refined.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da spoke concisely and thought with precision.

sentences.zh: 在軍，令出不二。

translations.literal: In the army, orders issued were not duplicated.
translations.idiomatic: In the field his orders brooked no second word.

sentences.zh: 諸將奉持凜凜，而帝前恭謹如不能言。

translations.literal: The generals held to him in awe, yet before the Emperor he was respectful and cautious as though unable to speak.
translations.idiomatic: His generals stood in awe of him, yet before the Emperor he was so deferential he seemed unable to speak.

sentences.zh: 善拊循，與下同甘苦，士無不感恩效死，以故所向克捷。

translations.literal: He was skilled in comforting and guiding, shared sweetness and bitterness with his subordinates; among the soldiers none failed to respond in gratitude and give their lives, and for this reason wherever he advanced he achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at winning men over and shared hardship with his troops; they repaid him with loyal service unto death, and for that reason he was victorious wherever he marched.

sentences.zh: 尤嚴戢部伍，所平大都二，省會三，郡邑百數，閭井宴然，民不苦兵。

translations.literal: He was especially strict in restraining his troops; of the great capitals he pacified two, provincial capitals three, and prefectures and counties by the hundreds; lanes and wells were tranquil, and the people did not suffer from the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially strict with his troops; he pacified two great capitals, three provincial seats, and hundreds of counties, and everywhere lanes and wells stayed calm so the people did not suffer from war.

sentences.zh: 歸朝之日，單車就舍，延禮儒生，談議終日，雍雍如也。

translations.literal: On the day he returned to court he came in a single cart to his lodging, extended courtesy to Confucian scholars, and discussed and deliberated all day with harmonious ease.
translations.idiomatic: On his returns to court he came in a single cart to his house, entertained scholars, and talked with them harmoniously all day.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗稱之曰：「受命而出，成功而旋，不矜不伐，婦女無所愛，財寶無所取，中正無疵，昭明乎日月，大將軍一人而已。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once praised him, saying: "Receiving the command he goes forth; achieving success he returns—neither proud nor boastful; no fondness for women; no taking of wealth and treasure; upright without flaw, bright as sun and moon—only the Grand General alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once said of him: "He goes forth on command and returns in victory, neither proud nor boastful; he takes no women and seizes no treasure; he is upright and without flaw, bright as the sun and moon—the Grand General alone is such a man.

sentences.zh: 子四：輝祖、添福、膺緒、增壽。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Huizu, Tianfu, Yingxu, and Zengshou.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Huizu, Tianfu, Yingxu, and Zengshou.

sentences.zh: 長女為文皇帝後，次代王妃，次安王妃。

translations.literal: The eldest daughter became empress to the Literary Emperor; the next was consort to the Prince of Dai; the next consort to the Prince of An.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest daughter became empress to the Literary Emperor; the next married the Prince of Dai; the next the Prince of An.

sentences.zh: 輝祖死逾月，成祖詔群臣：「輝祖與齊、黃輩謀危社稷。

translations.literal: More than a month after Huizu's death, the Yongle Emperor issued an edict to the ministers: "Huizu with Qi, Huang, and their ilk plotted to endanger the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month after Huizu's death, the Yongle Emperor told the ministers: "Huizu plotted with Qi, Huang, and their faction to endanger the realm.

sentences.zh: 朕念中山王有大功，曲赦之。

translations.literal: We, recalling that the Prince of Zhongshan had great merit, pardoned him by bending the law.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering the Prince of Zhongshan's great merit, I pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 今輝祖死，中山王不可無後。」

translations.literal: Now that Huizu is dead, the Prince of Zhongshan must not be without posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Huizu is dead, the Prince of Zhongshan must have an heir.

sentences.zh: 遂命輝祖長子欽嗣。

translations.literal: He then ordered Huizu's eldest son Qin to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Huizu's eldest son Qin to succeed.

sentences.zh: 九年，欽與成國公勇、定國公景昌、永康侯忠等，俱以縱恣為言官所劾。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Qin with the Duke of Cheng Yong, the Duke of Ding Jingchang, the Marquis of Yongkang Zhong, and others were all impeached by remonstrance officials for wanton license.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Qin, the Duke of Cheng Yong, the Duke of Ding Jingchang, the Marquis of Yongkang Zhong, and others were impeached by censors for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 帝宥勇等，而令欽歸就學。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned Yong and the others but ordered Qin to return and resume study.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pardoned Yong and the rest but sent Qin home to resume his studies.

sentences.zh: 十九年來朝，遽辭歸。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he came to court and abruptly took leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he came to court and abruptly left.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，罷為民。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and dismissed him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was angry and reduced him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，復故爵，傳子顯宗、承宗。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor acceded, his former rank was restored; it passed to his sons Xianzong and Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Renzong Emperor acceded, his title was restored; it passed to his sons Xianzong and Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 承宗，天順初，守備南京，兼領中軍府，公廉恤士有賢聲。

translations.literal: Chengzong, at the beginning of the Tianshun reign, garrisoned Nanjing and concurrently headed the Central Military Commission; he was fair, incorrupt, and sympathetic to officers and had a reputation for worth.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong, early in the Tianshun reign, held Nanjing and headed the Central Military Commission; his fairness and care for his men won him a reputation for virtue.

sentences.zh: 卒，子俌嗣。

translations.literal: He died; his son Fu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was succeeded by his son Fu.

sentences.zh: 俌字公輔，持重，善容止。

translations.literal: Fu, style name Gongfu, was weighty in bearing and skilled in deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, whose style name was Gongfu, was grave in manner and dignified in bearing.

sentences.zh: 南京守備體最隆，懷柔伯施钅監以協同守備位俌上。

translations.literal: The Nanjing garrison commander's ceremonial standing was the most exalted; the Earl of Huairou Shi Jian, as co-garrison commander, was ranked above Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing garrison commander's ceremonial standing was the highest; the Earl of Huairou Shi Jian, as co-commander, was ranked above Fu.

sentences.zh: 亻甫不平，言於朝，詔以爵為序，著為令。

translations.literal: Fu was displeased, spoke of it at court, and an edict ordered precedence by noble rank and made this a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Fu protested to the court; an edict ordered precedence by noble rank and made it a standing rule.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年，給事中胡易、御史胡獻以災異陳言下獄，俌上章救之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi the supervising secretary Hu Yi and censor Hu Xian, for memorializing on omens and disasters, were imprisoned; Fu submitted a memorial to save them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi the supervising secretary Hu Yi and the censor Hu Xian were imprisoned for memorializing on omens; Fu submitted a memorial in their defense.

sentences.zh: 正德中，上書諫遊畋，語切直。

translations.literal: During Zhengde he submitted a memorial remonstrating against hunting excursions; the language was cutting and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde he memorialized against the emperor's hunting, in blunt and forthright language.

sentences.zh: 嘗與無錫民爭田，賄劉瑾，為時所譏。

translations.literal: He once disputed fields with commoners of Wuxi and bribed Liu Jin, and was ridiculed by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: He once disputed land with commoners of Wuxi and bribed Liu Jin, for which he was widely scorned.

sentences.zh: 俌嗣五十二年而卒，贈太傅，諡莊靖。

translations.literal: Fu held the succession fifty-two years and then died; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor with posthumous name Zhuangjing.
translations.idiomatic: Fu held the title fifty-two years and died; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Zhuangjing.

sentences.zh: 孫鵬舉嗣，嬖其妾，冒封夫人，欲立其子為嫡，坐奪祿。

translations.literal: His grandson Pengju succeeded, favored his concubine, falsely enfeoffed her as lady, wished to establish her son as legitimate heir, and was punished by deprivation of stipend.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Pengju succeeded, favored a concubine, had her falsely ennobled as lady, and tried to make her son the heir; he was punished by loss of stipend.

sentences.zh: 傳子邦瑞，孫維志，曾孫弘基。

translations.literal: It passed to his son Bangrui, grandson Weizhi, and great-grandson Hongji.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed to his son Bangrui, grandson Weizhi, and great-grandson Hongji.

sentences.zh: 自承宗至弘基六世，皆守備南京，領軍府事。

translations.literal: From Chengzong to Hongji for six generations, all garrisoned Nanjing and headed military commission affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From Chengzong through Hongji for six generations, all held Nanjing and headed the military commission.

sentences.zh: 弘基累加太傅，卒，諡莊武，子文爵嗣。

translations.literal: Hongji was repeatedly promoted to Grand Tutor; on his death his posthumous name was Zhuangwu; his son Wenjue succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji rose to Grand Tutor, died with the posthumous name Zhuangwu, and was succeeded by his son Wenjue.

sentences.zh: 明亡，爵除。

translations.literal: When Ming perished, the noble rank was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming fell, the title was abolished.

sentences.zh: 增壽以父任仕至左都督。

translations.literal: Zengshou through his father's position served up to Left Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's influence Zengshou rose to Left Commissioner-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 建文帝疑燕王反，嘗以問增壽。

translations.literal: The Jianwen Emperor suspected the Prince of Yan of rebellion and once questioned Zengshou about it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jianwen Emperor suspected the Prince of Yan of rebellion, he once asked Zengshou.

sentences.zh: 增壽頓首曰：「燕王先帝同氣，富貴已極，何故反！」

translations.literal: Zengshou bowed his head and said: "The Prince of Yan shares the late Emperor's vital breath; his wealth and honor are already at the limit—why would he rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Zengshou kowtowed and said, "The Prince of Yan is the late Emperor's own brother, already at the height of wealth and honor—why would he rebel!

sentences.zh: 及燕師起，數以京師虛實輸于燕。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, he repeatedly reported the capital's strengths and weaknesses to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army rose, he repeatedly reported the capital's strengths and weaknesses to the prince.

sentences.zh: 帝覺之，未及問。

translations.literal: The Emperor became aware of it but had not yet questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor learned of it but had not yet questioned him.

sentences.zh: 比燕兵渡江，帝召增壽詰之，不對，手劍斬之殿廡下。

translations.literal: When the Yan troops crossed the river, the Emperor summoned Zengshou to interrogate him; he did not answer; the Emperor with his own hand beheaded him below the palace veranda.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army crossed the Yangzi, the Emperor summoned Zengshou and questioned him; he would not answer; the Emperor slew him with his own sword below the palace veranda.

sentences.zh: 王入，撫屍哭。

translations.literal: When the Prince entered, he caressed the corpse and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince entered the capital he embraced the body and wept.

sentences.zh: 即位，追封武陽侯，諡忠湣。

translations.literal: On acceding to the throne he posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuyang with posthumous name Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession he posthumously enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuyang with the posthumous name Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 尋進封定國公，祿二千五百石。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Duke of Ding with a stipend of twenty-five hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon advanced to Duke of Ding with a stipend of twenty-five hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 以其子景昌嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jingchang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingchang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 驕縱，數被劾，成祖輒宥之。

translations.literal: He was arrogant and unrestrained, repeatedly impeached, and the Yongle Emperor always pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrogant and repeatedly impeached, but the Yongle Emperor always pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 成祖崩，景昌坐居喪不出宿，奪冠服歲祿，已而復之。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor died, Jingchang was punished for not lodging out during mourning, lost cap, robes, and annual stipend, but later had them restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor died, Jingchang was punished for not leaving his quarters during mourning and lost his rank and stipend, but both were later restored.

sentences.zh: 三傳至玄孫光祚，累典軍府，加太師，嗣四十五年卒，諡榮僖。

translations.literal: After three transmissions to his great-great-grandson Guangzuo, who repeatedly headed military commissions and was made Grand Preceptor, he held the succession forty-five years and died with posthumous name Rongxi.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations later his great-great-grandson Guangzuo repeatedly headed the military commissions, rose to Grand Preceptor, held the title forty-five years, and died with the posthumous name Rongxi.

sentences.zh: 傳子至孫文璧，萬曆中，領後軍府。

translations.literal: It passed to his son and then grandson Wenbi; during Wanli he headed the Rear Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed to his son and grandson Wenbi, who under Wanli headed the Rear Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 以小心謹畏見親於帝，數代郊天，加太師。

translations.literal: Because of his careful caution he was cherished by the Emperor; for several generations he assisted at suburban sacrifices to Heaven and was made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: His caution won the emperor's favor; for several generations the family assisted at suburban sacrifices and rose to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 累上書請建儲，罷礦稅，釋逮系。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials requesting establishment of the heir, abolition of mining taxes, and release of those detained.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized to establish an heir, abolish mining taxes, and release prisoners.

sentences.zh: 嗣三十五年卒，諡康惠。

translations.literal: He held the succession thirty-five years and died with posthumous name Kanghui.
translations.idiomatic: He held the title thirty-five years and died with the posthumous name Kanghui.

sentences.zh: 再傳至曾孫允禎，崇禎末為流賊所殺。

translations.literal: After two more transmissions to his great-grandson Yunzhen, at the end of Chongzhen he was killed by roving bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Two generations later his great-grandson Yunzhen was killed by bandits at the end of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 洪武諸功臣，惟達子孫有二公，分居兩京。

translations.literal: Among the Hongwu meritorious ministers, only Da's descendants had two dukes, separately dwelling in the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Hongwu meritorious ministers, only Xu Da's line held two ducal titles, one family in each capital.

sentences.zh: 魏國之後多賢，而累朝恩數，定國常倍之。

translations.literal: The Wei state's descendants were mostly worthy, yet through successive reigns the measure of favor—the Ding state was often double.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei dukes produced many worthy men, yet through the dynasties the Ding line's favors were often twice as great.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中詔裁恩澤世封，有言定國功弗稱者，竟弗奪也。

translations.literal: In Jiajing an edict curtailed enfeoffments of favor and hereditary grants; some said the Ding state's merit did not match, yet in the end it was not taken away.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing an edict curtailed hereditary favors; some said the Ding title was undeserved, yet it was never revoked.

sentences.zh: 添福早卒。

translations.literal: Tianfu died early.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu died young.

sentences.zh: 膺緒，授尚寶司卿，累遷中軍都督僉事，奉朝請，世襲指揮使。

translations.literal: Yingxu was appointed Director of the Imperial Seals Office, was repeatedly promoted to Associate Commissioner of the Central Military Commission, attended court audiences, and hereditarily held commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Yingxu was appointed director of the Imperial Seals Office, rose to associate commissioner of the Central Military Commission, attended court, and held a hereditary commandant's post.

sentences.zh: 常遇春

translations.literal: Chang Yuchun
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun

sentences.zh: 常遇春，字伯仁，懷遠人。

translations.literal: Chang Yuchun, style name Boren, was a man of Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun, whose style name was Boren, came from Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 貌奇偉，勇力絕人，猿臂善射。

translations.literal: His appearance was strange and grand; his courage and strength surpassed others; with ape-like arms he was skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was striking in appearance, possessed superhuman strength, and with his long arms was a master archer.

sentences.zh: 初從劉聚為盜，察聚終無成，歸太祖于和陽。

translations.literal: At first he followed Liu Ju as a bandit; perceiving that Ju would in the end achieve nothing, he submitted to the Founder at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He had first followed the bandit Liu Ju, but seeing Ju would never succeed, he submitted to the Founder at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 未至，困臥田間，夢神人被甲擁盾呼曰：「起起，主君來。」

translations.literal: Before he arrived, weary he lay sleeping in the fields and dreamed a divine man in armor holding a shield calling: "Arise, arise—the lord comes.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived he fell asleep exhausted in a field and dreamed of a divine man in armor with a shield crying, "Rise, rise—the lord comes.

sentences.zh: 驚寤，而太祖適至，即迎拜。

translations.literal: Startled he awoke, and the Founder happened to arrive; he at once went forward to bow in welcome.
translations.idiomatic: He woke with a start just as the Founder arrived, and went forward to bow.

sentences.zh: 時至正十五年四月也。

translations.literal: It was then the fourth month of the fifteenth year of Zhizheng.
translations.idiomatic: It was the fourth month of the fifteenth year of Zhizheng.

sentences.zh: 無何，自請為前鋒。

translations.literal: Before long he himself requested to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he volunteered as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「汝特饑來就食耳，吾安得汝留也。」

translations.literal: The Founder said: "You have simply come in hunger to get food—how can I keep you?
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said, "You have only come hungry for a meal—how can I keep you?

sentences.zh: 遇春固請。

translations.literal: Yuchun firmly requested.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun pressed his request.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「俟渡江，事我未晚也。」

translations.literal: The Founder said: "Wait until we cross the river—serving me will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said, "Wait until we cross the river—it will not be too late to serve me then.

sentences.zh: 及兵薄牛渚磯，元兵陳磯上，舟距岸且三丈余，莫能登。

translations.literal: When the army pressed on Niuzhu Rock, Yuan troops were arrayed on the rock; the boats were more than three zhang from shore and none could board.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Niuzhu Rock, Yuan troops held the shore; the boats stood more than three zhang from land and no one could board.

sentences.zh: 遇春飛舸至，太祖麾之前。

translations.literal: Yuchun came in a flying boat; the Founder waved him forward.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun came up in a swift boat; the Founder waved him forward.

sentences.zh: 遇春應聲，奮戈直前。

translations.literal: Yuchun answered the call, brandished his halberd, and advanced straight ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun answered at once, brandished his halberd, and charged straight ahead.

sentences.zh: 敵接其戈，乘勢躍而上，大呼跳蕩，元軍披靡。

translations.literal: The enemy met his halberd; riding the momentum he leaped aboard, shouted loudly and leaped about, and the Yuan army collapsed before him.
translations.idiomatic: An enemy met his halberd; he used the leverage to leap aboard, shouting and leaping about, and the Yuan line broke before him.
