sentences.zh: 諸將乘之，遂拔採石，進取太平。

translations.literal: The generals rode the opportunity; they then captured Caishi and advanced to take Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals followed; they took Caishi and advanced on Taiping.

sentences.zh: 授總管府先鋒，進總管都督。

translations.literal: He was appointed vanguard of the Commandery Office and promoted to Commandery Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vanguard of the commandery office and promoted to commandery commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時將士妻子輜重皆在和州，元中丞蠻子海牙復以舟師襲據採石，道中梗。

translations.literal: At that time the officers' and soldiers' wives, children, and baggage were all at Hezhou; the Yuan vice censor-in-chief Manzi Haiya again with a fleet raided and seized Caishi, and the road was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The army's families and baggage were at Hezhou; the Yuan vice censor Manzi Haiya seized Caishi again by sea and cut the route.

sentences.zh: 太祖自將攻之，遣遇春多張疑兵分敵勢。

translations.literal: The Founder personally led troops to attack it and sent Yuchun to deploy many dummy forces to divide the enemy's strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder led the assault in person and sent Chang Yuchun to deploy decoys and divide the enemy.

sentences.zh: 戰既合，遇春操輕舸，沖海牙舟為二。

translations.literal: Once battle was joined, Yuchun manned a light boat and rammed Haiya's vessel in two.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined, Chang Yuchun in a light boat rammed Haiya's ship and split it in two.

sentences.zh: 左右縱擊，大敗之，盡得其舟。

translations.literal: To left and right he struck freely, utterly defeated them, and obtained all their boats.
translations.idiomatic: He struck from both sides, routed them, and seized their entire fleet.

sentences.zh: 江路復通。

translations.literal: The river route was open again.
translations.idiomatic: The river route was open again.

sentences.zh: 尋命守溧陽，從攻集慶，功最。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to garrison Liyang; he followed in attacking Jiqing with the foremost merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to hold Liyang and took the greatest credit in the assault on Jiqing.

sentences.zh: 從元帥徐達取鎮江，進取常州。

translations.literal: He followed Marshal Xu Da in taking Zhenjiang and advancing to seize Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Marshal Xu Da in taking Zhenjiang and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 吳兵圍達于牛塘，遇春往援，破解之，擒其將，進統軍大元帥。

translations.literal: Wu troops besieged Da at Niutang; Yuchun went to the rescue, broke and resolved the siege, captured their general, and was promoted to Grand Marshal Who Commands the Armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu forces besieged Xu Da at Niutang, Chang Yuchun relieved him, broke the siege, captured an enemy general, and was promoted to grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 克常州，遷中翼大元帥。

translations.literal: When Changzhou was captured he was transferred to Grand Marshal of the Central Wing.
translations.idiomatic: After Changzhou fell he was made grand marshal of the central wing.

sentences.zh: 從達攻甯國，中流矢，裹創鬥，克之。

translations.literal: He followed Da in attacking Ningguo, was struck by a stray arrow, wrapped his wound and fought, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xu Da against Ningguo, took an arrow, bound his wound, and fought on until the city fell.

sentences.zh: 別取馬駝沙，以舟師攻池州，下之，進行省都督馬步水軍大元帥。

translations.literal: Separately he took Matuosha; with a fleet he attacked Chizhou and reduced it; he was promoted to Grand Marshal of Cavalry, Infantry, and Naval Forces of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He separately took Matuosha, took Chizhou by water, and was promoted to grand marshal of horse, foot, and naval forces of the branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從取婺州，轉同僉樞密院事，守婺。

translations.literal: He followed in taking Wuzhou, was transferred to Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and garrisoned Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Wuzhou, was made associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and garrisoned the city.

sentences.zh: 移兵圍衢州，以奇兵突入南門甕城，毀其戰具，急攻之，遂下，得甲士萬人，進僉樞密院事。

translations.literal: He shifted troops to besiege Quzhou; with surprise troops he burst into the south gate barbican, destroyed their war equipment, pressed the attack urgently, and thereby reduced it, obtaining ten thousand armored soldiers; he was promoted to Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to besiege Quzhou, stormed the south gate barbican with a surprise force, destroyed their siege equipment, and took the city with ten thousand armored men; he was promoted to commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 攻杭州，失利，召還應天。

translations.literal: Attacking Hangzhou he met ill fortune and was recalled to Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: An attack on Hangzhou failed and he was recalled to Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 從達拔趙普勝之水寨，從守池州，大破漢兵于九華山下，語具《達傳》。

translations.literal: He followed Da in capturing Zhao Pusheng's water stockade, followed in garrisoning Chizhou, and utterly defeated Han troops below Mount Jiuhua—the account is fully set forth in the Da biography.
translations.idiomatic: He helped Xu Da take Zhao Pusheng's river camp, held Chizhou, and routed the Han army below Mount Jiuhua—the full account is in Xu Da's biography.

sentences.zh: 友諒薄龍灣，遇春以五翼軍設伏，大破之，遂復太平，功最。

translations.literal: Youliang pressed on Longwan; Yuchun with five-wing armies set an ambush and utterly defeated him, then recovered Taiping with the foremost merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Youliang pressed Longwan, Chang Yuchun ambushed him with five divisions, routed him, and recovered Taiping with the greatest credit.

sentences.zh: 太祖追友諒于江州，命遇春留守，用法嚴，軍民肅然無敢犯，進行省參知政事。

translations.literal: The Founder pursued Youliang at Jiangzhou and ordered Yuchun to remain on garrison; his application of law was strict, army and people were awed and none dared violate; he was promoted to Branch Secretariat Participating Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founder pursued Youliang to Jiangzhou, Chang Yuchun held the base with such strict discipline that none dared offend; he was promoted to participating administrator of the branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從取安慶。

translations.literal: He followed in taking Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Anqing.

sentences.zh: 漢軍出江遊徼，遇春擊之，皆反走，乘勝取江州。

translations.literal: Han troops came out on the river on patrol; Yuchun struck them and all turned back in flight; riding victory he took Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Han troops patrolled the river, Chang Yuchun routed them and pressed on to take Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 還守龍灣，援長興，俘殺吳兵五千餘人，其將李伯升解圍遁。

translations.literal: Returning he garrisoned Longwan, relieved Changxing, captured and killed more than five thousand Wu troops, and their general Li Bosheng lifted the siege and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Longwan he relieved Changxing, killed or captured more than five thousand Wu troops, and their general Li Bosheng lifted the siege and fled.

sentences.zh: 命甓安慶城。

translations.literal: He was ordered to brick the walls of Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to rebuild the walls of Anqing with brick.

sentences.zh: 先是，太祖所任將帥最著者，平章邵榮、右丞徐達與遇春為三。

translations.literal: Earlier, among the commanders the Founder appointed the most renowned were Pingzhang Shao Rong, Right Chancellor Xu Da, and Yuchun as three.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Founder's foremost commanders had been Pingzhang Shao Rong, Right Chancellor Xu Da, and Chang Yuchun.

sentences.zh: 而榮尤宿將善戰，至是驕蹇有異志，與參政趙繼祖謀伏兵為變。

translations.literal: But Rong was especially a veteran skilled in battle; by now he was arrogant and obstinate with a different intent, and with Participating Administrator Zhao Jizu plotted to set hidden troops for a mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was an old hand especially skilled in battle, but by now he had grown arrogant and, with Participating Administrator Zhao Jizu, plotted a mutiny with hidden troops.

sentences.zh: 事覺，太祖欲宥榮死，遇春直前曰：「人臣以反名，尚何可宥，臣義不與共生。」

translations.literal: When the matter was discovered, the Founder wished to spare Rong from death; Yuchun advanced straight forward and said: "A subject bearing the name of rebel—how can he still be pardoned? Your subject's duty does not permit living together with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered the Founder wished to spare Rong; Chang Yuchun stepped forward and said, "A subject who bears the name of rebel—how can he be pardoned? I cannot live while he lives.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃飲榮酒，流涕而戮之，以是益愛重遇春。

translations.literal: The Founder then had Rong drink wine, wept as he executed him, and for this valued Yuchun all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder gave Rong wine, wept as he executed him, and thereafter valued Chang Yuchun all the more.

sentences.zh: 池州帥羅友賢據神山寨，通張士誠，遇春破斬之。

translations.literal: The Chizhou commander Luo Youxian held Divine Mountain Stockade, communicated with Zhang Shicheng; Yuchun broke his force and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The Chizhou commander Luo Youxian held Divine Mountain Stockade in league with Zhang Shicheng; Chang Yuchun defeated and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 從援安豐。

translations.literal: He followed in relieving Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the relief of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 比至，呂珍已陷其城，殺劉福通，聞大軍至，盛兵拒守。

translations.literal: By the time they arrived Lü Zhen had already seized its city and killed Liu Futong; hearing the great army had come, he massed troops to resist and hold.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they arrived Lü Zhen had already taken the city and killed Liu Futong; hearing the main army was coming, he massed his forces to resist.

sentences.zh: 太祖左右軍皆敗，遇春橫擊其陣，三戰三破之，俘獲士馬無算。

translations.literal: The Founder's left and right armies were all defeated; Yuchun struck across their battle line, three times fought and three times broke them, and captured officers, soldiers, horses, and equipment beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Both wings of the Founder's army were beaten; Chang Yuchun struck across the enemy line, broke them three times running, and took prisoners and horses beyond count.

sentences.zh: 遂從達圍廬州。

translations.literal: He then followed Da in besieging Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Xu Da in besieging Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 城將下，陳友諒圍洪都，召還。

translations.literal: When the city was about to fall, Chen Youliang besieged Hongdu and he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall, Chen Youliang besieged Hongdu and he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 會師伐漢，遇于彭蠡之康郎山。

translations.literal: The armies united to campaign against Han and met at Kanglang Mountain on Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: The armies united against Han and met at Kanglang Mountain on Lake Poyang.

sentences.zh: 漢軍舟大，乘上流，鋒銳甚。

translations.literal: The Han army's boats were large; riding the upper current, their edge was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: The Han fleet was large and held the upstream current; their vanguard was fierce.

sentences.zh: 遇春偕諸將大戰，呼聲動天地，無不一當百。

translations.literal: Yuchun with the generals fought a great battle; their shouts shook heaven and earth; none failed to match a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun and the generals fought a great battle; their shouts shook heaven and earth; each man fought as ten.

sentences.zh: 友諒驍將張定邊直犯太祖舟，舟膠於淺，幾殆。

translations.literal: Youliang's fierce general Zhang Dingbian struck straight at the Founder's boat; the boat stuck in shallows and was nearly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang's fierce general Zhang Dingbian drove straight at the Founder's boat, which grounded in the shallows and was nearly lost.

sentences.zh: 遇春射中定邊，太祖舟得脫，而遇春舟復膠於淺。

translations.literal: Yuchun shot and hit Dingbian; the Founder's boat was able to escape, but Yuchun's boat again stuck in shallows.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun shot Dingbian; the Founder's boat escaped, but Chang Yuchun's grounded again.

sentences.zh: 有敗舟順流下，觸遇春舟乃脫。

translations.literal: A defeated boat drifted downstream with the current, struck Yuchun's boat, and only then was he freed.
translations.idiomatic: A wreck drifting downstream struck his boat and freed it.

sentences.zh: 轉戰三日，縱火焚漢舟，湖水皆赤，友諒不敢復戰。

translations.literal: They fought on for three days; they set fire and burned Han boats; the lake water all turned red; Youliang did not dare fight again.
translations.idiomatic: After three days of fighting they burned the Han fleet; the lake ran red, and Youliang dared not fight again.

sentences.zh: 諸將以漢軍尚強，欲縱之去，遇春獨無言。

translations.literal: The generals, because the Han army was still strong, wished to let them go; Yuchun alone said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The generals, judging the Han army still strong, wished to let them go; Chang Yuchun alone said nothing.

sentences.zh: 比出湖口，諸將欲放舟東下，太祖命扼上流。

translations.literal: When they reached the lake mouth, the generals wished to release the boats and go east downstream; the Founder ordered them to hold the upper current.
translations.idiomatic: At the lake mouth the generals wished to sail east downstream; the Founder ordered them to hold the upper current.

sentences.zh: 遇春乃溯江而上，諸將從之。

translations.literal: Yuchun then went upriver against the current and the generals followed.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun rowed upriver and the generals followed.

sentences.zh: 友諒窮蹙，以百艘突圍。

translations.literal: Youliang, pressed to extremity, broke out with a hundred boats.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang, desperate, broke out with a hundred boats.

sentences.zh: 諸將邀擊之，漢軍遂大潰，友諒死。

translations.literal: The generals intercepted and struck them; the Han army then utterly collapsed and Youliang died.
translations.idiomatic: The generals intercepted them; the Han army collapsed and Youliang was killed.

sentences.zh: 師還，第功最，賚金帛土田甚厚。

translations.literal: When the army returned, his merit was ranked first; he was bestowed gold, silks, and land fields in great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return his merit ranked first and he was rewarded lavishly with gold, silk, and land.

sentences.zh: 從圍武昌，太祖還應天，留遇春督軍困之。

translations.literal: He followed in besieging Wuchang; the Founder returned to Yingtian and left Yuchun to supervise the army in pressing it.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the siege of Wuchang; the Founder returned to Yingtian and left Chang Yuchun to press the siege.

sentences.zh: 明年，太祖即吳王位，進遇春平章政事。

translations.literal: The next year the Founder assumed the title King of Wu and promoted Yuchun to Pingzhang Administrator of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Founder became King of Wu and promoted Chang Yuchun to pingzhang administrator of affairs.

sentences.zh: 太祖復視師武昌。

translations.literal: The Founder again inspected the army at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder again inspected the army at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 漢丞相張必先自嶽來援。

translations.literal: The Han chancellor Zhang Bixian came from Yue to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The Han chancellor Zhang Bixian marched from Yue to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 遇春乘其未集，急擊擒之。

translations.literal: Yuchun, riding their failure to assemble, pressed the attack urgently and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun struck before they could assemble and captured him.

sentences.zh: 城中由是氣奪，陳理遂降，盡取荊、湖地。

translations.literal: Within the city morale was thereby seized away; Chen Li then surrendered and they entirely took the Jing and Hu regions.
translations.idiomatic: The city's morale collapsed; Chen Li surrendered and the Jing and Hu regions were taken.

sentences.zh: 從左相國達取廬州，別將兵略定臨江之沙坑、麻嶺、牛陂諸寨，擒偽知州鄧克明，遂下吉安。

translations.literal: He followed Left Prime Minister Da in taking Luzhou, separately led troops to overrun and settle the stockades of Shaken, Maling, and Niupo in Linjiang, captured the false prefect Deng Keming, and thereby reduced Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Left Prime Minister Xu Da in taking Luzhou, separately reduced the stockades of Shaken, Maling, and Niupo in Linjiang, captured the rebel prefect Deng Keming, and took Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 圍贛州，熊天瑞固守不下。

translations.literal: He besieged Ganzhou; Xiong Tianrui firmly held and would not be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Ganzhou, but Xiong Tianrui held firm and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 太祖使使諭遇春：「克城無多殺。

translations.literal: The Founder sent an envoy to instruct Yuchun: "In capturing a city do not kill many.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent word to Chang Yuchun: "When you take a city, do not slaughter the people.

sentences.zh: 苟得地，無民何益？」

translations.literal: If one obtains land but has no people, what benefit is there?
translations.idiomatic: What good is land without people?

sentences.zh: 於是遇春浚壕立柵以困之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuchun dredged moats and set palisades to press him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun then dug moats and built palisades to wear the city down.

sentences.zh: 頓兵六月，天瑞力盡乃降，遇春果不殺。

translations.literal: The army halted six months; when Tianrui's strength was exhausted he surrendered; Yuchun indeed did not kill.
translations.idiomatic: After six months Tianrui's strength gave out and he surrendered; Chang Yuchun spared him as promised.

sentences.zh: 太祖大喜，賜書褒勉。

translations.literal: The Founder was greatly pleased and bestowed a letter of praise and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was delighted and sent a letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 遇春遂因兵威諭降南雄、韶州，還定安陸、襄陽。

translations.literal: Yuchun then by military might instructed and received the surrender of Nanxiong and Shaozhou, and returned to settle Anlu and Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun then overawed Nanxiong and Shaozhou into surrender and pacified Anlu and Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 復從徐達克泰州，敗士誠援兵，督水軍壁海安壩以遏之。

translations.literal: He again followed Xu Da in capturing Taizhou, defeated Shicheng's relief troops, and supervised the naval army in fortifying at Hai'an Dam to block them.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Xu Da in taking Taizhou, routed Zhang Shicheng's relief force, and posted the fleet at Hai'an Dam to block them.

sentences.zh: 其秋拜副將軍，伐吳。

translations.literal: That autumn he was appointed vice general and campaigned against Wu.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was made deputy general for the campaign against Wu.

sentences.zh: 敗吳軍於太湖，於毘山，於三里橋，遂薄湖州。

translations.literal: He defeated Wu troops at Lake Tai, at Pishan, and at Sanli Bridge, then pressed on Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Wu forces at Lake Tai, Pishan, and Sanli Bridge, then pressed on Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 士誠遣兵來援，屯於舊館，出大軍後。

translations.literal: Shicheng sent troops to the rescue, encamped at Jiuguan, and came out behind the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng sent relief troops to Jiuguan, coming up behind the main army.

sentences.zh: 遇春將奇兵由大全港營東阡，更出其後。

translations.literal: Yuchun led surprise troops from Daquan Harbor to encamp at East Qian and again came out behind them.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun led a flanking force from Daquan Harbor to East Qian and again got behind the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵出精卒搏戰，奮擊破之。

translations.literal: The enemy sent out elite soldiers to grapple in battle; he fought fiercely and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sent elite troops to fight; he struck fiercely and broke them.

sentences.zh: 襲其右丞徐義于平望，盡燔其赤龍船，復敗之于烏鎮，逐北至升山，破其水陸寨，悉俘舊館兵，湖州遂下。

translations.literal: He raided their right chancellor Xu Yi at Pingwang and burned all their Red Dragon boats; again defeated them at Wuzhen, pursued north to Shengshan, broke their land and water stockades, entirely captured the Jiuguan troops, and Huzhou was thereby reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He raided their right chancellor Xu Yi at Pingwang and burned the Red Dragon fleet, routed them again at Wuzhen, pursued north to Shengshan, broke their camps by land and water, captured the Jiuguan force, and Huzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 進圍平江，軍虎丘。

translations.literal: Advancing he besieged Pingjiang with his army at Tiger Hill.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to besiege Pingjiang from Tiger Hill.

sentences.zh: 士誠潛師趨遇春，遇春與戰北濠，破之，幾獲士誠。

translations.literal: Shicheng with hidden troops rushed toward Yuchun; Yuchun fought him at North Moat, broke him, and nearly captured Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng sent a stealth force against Chang Yuchun; at North Moat Chang Yuchun routed them and nearly captured Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 久之，諸將破葑門，遇春亦破閶門以入，吳平。

translations.literal: After long time the generals broke the Fumeng Gate; Yuchun also broke the Chang Gate to enter; Wu was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: At last the generals broke the Fumeng Gate; Chang Yuchun broke the Chang Gate and entered; Wu was pacified.

sentences.zh: 進中書平章軍國重事，封鄂國公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat Pingzhang for Weighty Affairs of Army and State and enfeoffed as Duke of E.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretariat pingzhang for weighty military and state affairs and enfeoffed as Duke of E.

sentences.zh: 復拜副將軍，與大將軍達帥兵北征。

translations.literal: He was again appointed vice general and with Grand General Da commanded troops on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made deputy general and marched north with Grand General Xu Da.

sentences.zh: 帝親諭曰：「當百萬眾，摧鋒陷堅，莫如副將軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally instructed him, saying: "Facing a million men, crushing the vanguard and storming strongholds—none matches the vice general.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told him in person: "Against a million men, none breaks the vanguard and storms strongholds like you.

sentences.zh: 不慮不能戰，慮輕戰耳。

translations.literal: I do not worry that you cannot fight; I worry that you fight lightly.
translations.idiomatic: I do not doubt you can fight—I fear you fight too lightly.

sentences.zh: 身為大將，顧好與小校角，甚非所望也。」

translations.literal: Bearing the body of a great general, yet fond of wrestling with junior officers—that is very far from what is hoped.
translations.idiomatic: As a great general you still love to wrestle junior officers—that is not what I want of you.

sentences.zh: 遇春拜謝。

translations.literal: Yuchun bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun bowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 既行，以遇春兼太子少保，從下山東諸郡，取汴梁，進攻河南。

translations.literal: After he marched, Yuchun was made concurrent Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; he followed in reducing the Shandong prefectures, took Bianliang, and advanced to attack Henan.
translations.idiomatic: On the march he was made concurrent junior tutor to the heir apparent; he helped reduce Shandong, took Bianliang, and advanced into Henan.

sentences.zh: 元兵五萬陳洛水北。

translations.literal: Fifty thousand Yuan troops were arrayed north of the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty thousand Yuan troops stood north of the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 遇春單騎突其陣，敵二十餘騎攢朔刺之。

translations.literal: Yuchun on a single horse burst into their battle line; more than twenty enemy horsemen gathered and stabbed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun charged their line alone; more than twenty enemy horsemen surrounded and stabbed at him.

sentences.zh: 遇春一矢殪其前鋒，大呼馳入，麾下壯士從之。

translations.literal: Yuchun with one arrow killed their vanguard, shouted loudly and galloped in, and the stalwart men under his command followed.
translations.idiomatic: With one arrow he killed their vanguard, shouted, and charged in; his stalwarts followed.

sentences.zh: 敵大潰，追奔五十餘里。

translations.literal: The enemy utterly collapsed; they pursued the fleeing foe more than fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy collapsed and was pursued more than fifty li.

sentences.zh: 降梁王阿魯溫，河南郡邑以次下。

translations.literal: The Liang prince Aruwen surrendered; Henan's prefectures and counties were reduced in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang prince Aruwen surrendered and Henan's cities fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 謁帝於汴梁，遂與大將軍下河北諸郡。

translations.literal: He had an audience with the Emperor at Bianliang, then with the Grand General reduced the Hebei prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He had audience with the Emperor at Bianliang, then with the Grand General reduced the Hebei prefectures.

sentences.zh: 先驅取德州，將舟師並河而進，破元兵於河西務，克通州，遂入元都。

translations.literal: As vanguard he took Dezhou, led the fleet along the river in advance, defeated Yuan troops at Hexiwu, captured Tongzhou, and thereby entered the Yuan capital.
translations.idiomatic: As vanguard he took Dezhou, led the fleet upriver, routed the Yuan at Hexiwu, took Tongzhou, and entered Dadu.

sentences.zh: 別下保定、河間、真定。

translations.literal: Separately he reduced Baoding, Hejian, and Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He separately took Baoding, Hejian, and Zhending.

sentences.zh: 與大將軍攻太原，擴廓帖木兒來援。

translations.literal: With the Grand General he attacked Taiyuan; Köke Temür came to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: With the Grand General he attacked Taiyuan; Köke Temür came to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 遇春言于達曰：「我騎兵雖集，步卒未至，驟與戰必多殺傷，夜劫之可得志。」

translations.literal: Yuchun said to Da: "Our cavalry though gathered, the infantry have not arrived; if we fight suddenly there will surely be many killed and wounded—raiding by night we can achieve our aim.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun said to Xu Da, "Our cavalry is here but the infantry has not arrived—a sudden fight would cost many lives; a night raid will succeed.

sentences.zh: 達曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Da said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da said, "Good."

sentences.zh: 會擴廓部將豁鼻馬來約降，且請為內應，乃選精騎夜銜枚往襲。

translations.literal: It happened that Köke Temür's subordinate general Huobima came to arrange surrender and also requested to serve as inner collaborator; they then selected crack cavalry who by night with gag-sticks in their mouths went to raid.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür's lieutenant Huobima offered to surrender and act as informant; they chose elite cavalry and raided by night with gag-sticks in their mouths.

sentences.zh: 擴廓方燃燭治軍書，倉卒不知所出，跣一足，乘孱馬，以十八騎走大同。

translations.literal: Köke Temür was just by candlelight handling military documents; in haste he knew not what to do; barefoot on one foot he mounted a weak horse and with eighteen horsemen fled to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Köke Temür was by candlelight writing orders when the raid struck; he fled barefoot on a weak horse with eighteen men to Datong.

sentences.zh: 豁鼻馬降，得甲士四萬，遂克太原。

translations.literal: Huobima surrendered; they obtained forty thousand armored soldiers and thereby captured Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huobima surrendered; they took forty thousand armored men and captured Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 遇春追擴廓至忻州而還。

translations.literal: Yuchun pursued Köke Temür to Xinzhou and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun pursued Köke Temür to Xinzhou and returned.

sentences.zh: 詔改遇春左副將軍，居右副將軍馮勝上。

translations.literal: An edict changed Yuchun to left vice general, ranking above right vice general Feng Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Chang Yuchun left deputy general, ranking above the right deputy Feng Sheng.

sentences.zh: 北取大同，轉徇河東，下奉元路，與勝軍合，西拔鳳翔。

translations.literal: Northward he took Datong, turned to march through Hedong, reduced Fengyuan Circuit, united with Sheng's army, and westward seized Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He took Datong, swept Hedong, reduced Fengyuan, joined Feng Sheng, and took Fengxiang in the west.

sentences.zh: 會元將也速攻通州，詔遇春還備，以平章李文忠副之，帥步騎九萬，發北平，徑會州，敗敵將江文清於錦州，敗也速于全寧。

translations.literal: It happened that the Yuan general Yesü attacked Tongzhou; an edict ordered Yuchun back on defense; with Pingzhang Li Wenzhong as deputy he commanded ninety thousand infantry and cavalry, set out from Beiping, went straight to Huizhou, defeated the enemy general Jiang Wenqing at Jinzhou, and defeated Yesü at Quanning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan general Yesü attacked Tongzhou, Chang Yuchun was recalled; with Li Wenzhong as deputy he led ninety thousand foot and horse from Beiping, defeated Jiang Wenqing at Jinzhou and Yesü at Quanning.

sentences.zh: 進攻大興州，分千騎為八伏。

translations.literal: Advancing he attacked Daxing Prefecture and divided a thousand horsemen into eight ambushes.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Daxing Prefecture with a thousand horsemen in eight ambushes.

sentences.zh: 守將夜遁，盡擒之，遂拔開平。

translations.literal: The defending general fled by night; all were captured; he then took Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: The defender fled by night and was captured; Kaiping fell.

sentences.zh: 元帝北走，追奔數百里。

translations.literal: The Yuan emperor fled north; they pursued the fleeing foe several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan emperor fled north and was pursued for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 獲其宗王慶生及平章鼎住等將士萬人，車萬輛，馬三千匹，牛五萬頭，子女寶貨稱是。

translations.literal: They captured his imperial prince Qingsheng and pingzhang Dingzhu and more than ten thousand officers and soldiers, ten thousand carts, three thousand horses, fifty thousand cattle, and wives, children, treasures, and goods in full measure.
translations.idiomatic: They captured the imperial prince Qingsheng, the pingzhang Dingzhu, and ten thousand officers and men, ten thousand carts, three thousand horses, fifty thousand cattle, and women, children, and treasure in abundance.

sentences.zh: 師還，次柳河川，暴疾卒，年僅四十。

translations.literal: When the army returned it halted at Liuhe River; he died suddenly of acute illness, aged only forty.
translations.idiomatic: On the return the army halted at Liuhe River; he died suddenly of illness at only forty.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，大震悼。

translations.literal: When the Founder heard it he was greatly shocked and grieved.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was deeply shaken and grieved.

sentences.zh: 喪至龍江，親出奠，命禮官議天子為大臣發哀禮。

translations.literal: When the funeral procession reached Longjiang he personally went out to offer libation and ordered the ritual officials to deliberate on the rites for the Son of Heaven to mourn a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral reached Longjiang he went out in person to mourn and ordered the ritual officials to devise rites for the Son of Heaven to mourn a great minister.

sentences.zh: 議上，用宋太宗喪韓王趙普故事。

translations.literal: When the deliberation was submitted, they used the precedent of Song Taizong mourning Prince Han Zhao Pu.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed the precedent of Song Taizong mourning Prince Han Zhao Pu.

sentences.zh: 制曰「可」。

translations.literal: The decree said "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The decree approved it.

sentences.zh: 賜葬鐘山原，給明器九十事納墓中。

translations.literal: He was bestowed burial on Bell Mountain's plain; ninety sets of mingqi were given to be placed in the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried on the Bell Mountain plain with ninety sets of grave goods placed in the tomb.

sentences.zh: 贈翊運推誠宣德靖遠功臣、開府儀同三司、上柱國、太保、中書右丞相，追封開平王，諡忠武。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Meritorious Minister Who Assisted Fortune, Pushed Forward Sincerity, Proclaimed Virtue, and Pacified the Distance; Grand Preceptor of the Palace with Ceremonies Equal to the Three Excellencies; Supreme Pillar of the State; Grand Guardian; Right Chancellor of the Secretariat; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Kaiping with posthumous name Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made meritorious minister who assisted fortune with sincere virtue and pacified the frontier, grand preceptor of the palace with ceremonies equal to the three excellencies, supreme pillar of the state, grand guardian, and right chancellor of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Prince of Kaiping with the posthumous name Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 配享太廟，肖像功臣廟，位皆第二。

translations.literal: He received paired sacrifice in the Grand Temple; his portrait in the Meritorious Ministers Temple—both places second in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He received paired sacrifice in the Grand Temple and second place in the Meritorious Ministers Temple.

sentences.zh: 遇春沉鷙果敢，善撫士卒，摧鋒陷陣，未嘗敗北。

translations.literal: Yuchun was deep, stern, and resolute and daring; skilled in comforting troops; crushing the vanguard and storming battle lines—he never once met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun was deep, stern, and fearless, skilled at winning over his men; he broke vanguards and stormed battle lines and was never defeated.

sentences.zh: 雖不習書史，用兵輒與古合。

translations.literal: Though he did not study books and histories, in employing troops he invariably accorded with antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had not studied the classics, his use of troops invariably matched the ancients.

sentences.zh: 長於大將軍達二歲，數從征伐，聽約束惟謹，一時名將稱徐、常。

translations.literal: Two years older than Grand General Da, he repeatedly followed in campaigns and expeditions, heard constraints with sole care, and among the famed generals of the age they were called Xu and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Two years older than Grand General Xu Da, he campaigned repeatedly under strict discipline; the age's greatest generals were called Xu and Chang.

sentences.zh: 遇春嘗自言能將十萬眾，橫行天下，軍中又稱「常十萬」雲。

translations.literal: Yuchun once said himself that he could command a hundred thousand masses and march across the realm; in the army they also called him "Chang the Hundred Thousand."
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun once said he could lead a hundred thousand men and sweep the realm; the army called him "Chang the Hundred Thousand."

sentences.zh: 遇春從弟榮，積功為指揮同知，從李文忠出塞，戰死臚朐河。

translations.literal: Yuchun's younger cousin Rong, accumulating merit became commandant-in-chief; he followed Li Wenzhong beyond the passes and died in battle at Luju River.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun's cousin Rong rose to commandant-in-chief, followed Li Wenzhong beyond the frontier, and died at Luju River.

sentences.zh: 遇春二子，茂、升。

translations.literal: Yuchun had two sons: Mao and Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun had two sons: Mao and Sheng.

sentences.zh: 茂以遇春功，封鄭國公，食祿二千石，予世券，驕稚不習事。

translations.literal: Mao through Yuchun's merit was enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng with a stipend of two thousand piculs and granted a hereditary patent; he was arrogant, childish, and did not learn affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's merit Mao was enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng with two thousand piculs and a hereditary patent; he was arrogant and ignorant of affairs.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十年命從大將軍馮勝征納哈出於金山。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Hongwu he was ordered to follow Grand General Feng Sheng in campaigning against Naghachu at Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Hongwu he was ordered to follow Grand General Feng Sheng against Naghachu at Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 勝，茂婦翁也。

translations.literal: Sheng was Mao's father-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Sheng was Mao's father-in-law.

sentences.zh: 茂多不奉勝約束，勝數誚責之。

translations.literal: Mao often did not follow Sheng's constraints; Sheng repeatedly reproached and blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: Mao often ignored Feng Sheng's orders; Feng Sheng repeatedly rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 茂應之慢，勝益怒，未有以發也。

translations.literal: Mao answered him slowly; Sheng grew angrier but had no means to act.
translations.idiomatic: Mao answered insolently; Feng Sheng grew angrier but had no occasion to act.

sentences.zh: 會納哈出請降，詣右副將軍藍玉營，酒次，與玉相失，納哈出取酒澆地，顧其下咄咄語。

translations.literal: It happened that Naghachu requested surrender and came to Right Vice General Lan Yu's camp; during wine he and Yu fell out; Naghachu took wine and poured it on the ground, turned to his subordinates and spoke in urgent tones.
translations.idiomatic: When Naghachu came to surrender at Right Deputy Lan Yu's camp, he quarreled with Lan Yu over wine, poured wine on the ground, and spoke urgently to his men.

sentences.zh: 茂方在坐，麾下趙指揮者，解蒙古語，密告茂：「納哈出將遁矣。」

translations.literal: Mao was just seated there; a Commander Zhao under him understood Mongolian and secretly told Mao: "Naghachu is about to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was present; his officer Zhao understood Mongolian and whispered to Mao, "Naghachu is about to flee.

sentences.zh: 茂因出不意，直前搏之。

translations.literal: Mao therefore by unexpected move advanced straight forward and grappled with him.
translations.idiomatic: Mao seized him by surprise and grappled with him.

sentences.zh: 納哈出大驚，起欲就馬。

translations.literal: Naghachu was greatly startled, rose and wished to reach his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Naghachu was startled and rose to reach his horse.

sentences.zh: 茂拔刀，砍其臂傷。

translations.literal: Mao drew his blade and hacked his arm, wounding him.
translations.idiomatic: Mao drew his sword and cut his arm.

sentences.zh: 納哈出所部聞之，有驚潰者。

translations.literal: Naghachu's subordinates hearing it, some were alarmed and collapsed in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Some of Naghachu's men panicked and fled.

sentences.zh: 勝故怒茂，增飾其狀，奏茂激變，遂械系至京。

translations.literal: Sheng, already angry at Mao, embellished the account and memorialized that Mao had provoked a mutiny; he was then shackled and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Sheng, already angry at Mao, embellished the affair and reported that Mao had provoked a revolt; Mao was shackled and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 茂亦言勝諸不法事。

translations.literal: Mao also spoke of Sheng's various unlawful matters.
translations.idiomatic: Mao in turn accused Feng Sheng of various misconduct.

sentences.zh: 帝收勝總兵印，而安置茂于龍州，二十四年卒。

translations.literal: The Emperor took back Sheng's seal as commander-in-chief and settled Mao at Longzhou; in the twenty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took Feng Sheng's command seal and settled Mao at Longzhou; Mao died in the twenty-fourth year.

sentences.zh: 初，龍州土官趙貼堅死，從子宗壽當襲。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Longzhou native official Zhao Tiejian died; his nephew Zongshou should have inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Longzhou native official Zhao Tiejian had died; his nephew Zongshou should have succeeded.

sentences.zh: 貼堅妻黃以愛女予茂為小妻，擅州事。

translations.literal: Tiejian's wife Huang gave her beloved daughter to Mao as a minor wife and usurped prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tiejian's widow Huang gave her daughter to Mao as a concubine and usurped control of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 茂既死，黃與宗壽爭州印，相告訐。

translations.literal: When Mao had died, Huang and Zongshou disputed the prefectural seal and accused each other.
translations.idiomatic: After Mao's death Huang and Zongshou fought over the prefectural seal and denounced each other.

sentences.zh: 或構蜚語，謂茂實不死，宗壽知狀。

translations.literal: Some fabricated slanderous words, saying Mao in fact had not died and Zongshou knew the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that Mao was not really dead and that Zongshou knew it.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，責令獻茂自贖，命楊文、韓觀出師討龍州。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry, blamed them and ordered them to present Mao to redeem themselves, and commanded Yang Wen and Han Guan to march out and campaign against Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious, demanded Mao be produced, and sent Yang Wen and Han Guan against Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 已而知茂果死，宗壽亦輸款，乃罷兵。

translations.literal: Afterward they learned Mao had indeed died and Zongshou also submitted allegiance; the troops were then withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: When it was learned Mao was truly dead and Zongshou submitted, the army was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 茂無子，弟升，改封開國公，數出練軍，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Mao had no sons; his younger brother Sheng was changed to enfeoffment as Duke Who Founded the State, repeatedly went out to drill troops, and was made concurrent Junior Guardian to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Mao had no sons; his brother Sheng was made Duke Who Founded the State, repeatedly drilled troops on campaign, and rose to junior guardian to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 升之沒，《實錄》不載。

translations.literal: Sheng's death is not recorded in the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's death is not recorded in the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 其他書紀傳謂，建文末，升及魏國公輝祖力戰浦子口，死于永樂初。

translations.literal: Other books' chronicles and biographies say that at the end of Jianwen, Sheng and the Duke of Wei Huizu fought fiercely at Puzikou and died at the beginning of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: Other histories say that at the end of the Jianwen reign Sheng and the Duke of Wei Huizu fought fiercely at Puzikou and died early in Yongle.

sentences.zh: 或謂升洪武中坐藍玉黨，有告其聚兵三山者，誅死。

translations.literal: Some say that in Hongwu Sheng sat with the Lan Yu faction, someone reported that he gathered troops at Sanshan, and he was executed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Others say that in Hongwu he was implicated in the Lan Yu faction, was reported for gathering troops at Sanshan, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 常氏為興宗外戚，建文時恩禮宜厚，事遭革除，無可考，其死亦遂傳聞異詞。

translations.literal: The Chang clan were maternal kin to the Heir Apparent; in Jianwen times favor and ritual ought to have been thick; the affair suffered eradication and cannot be examined; his death also thus has differing words in rumor.
translations.idiomatic: The Chang clan were kin to the heir apparent; under Jianwen they should have enjoyed great favor, but records were destroyed in the purge, and even Sheng's death is reported in conflicting accounts.

sentences.zh: 升子繼祖，永樂元年遷雲南之臨安衛，時甫七歲。

translations.literal: Sheng's son Jizu, in the first year of Yongle was relocated to Yunnan's Lin'an Guard; he was then only seven.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's son Jizu was relocated to Lin'an Guard in Yunnan in the first year of Yongle, when he was only seven.

sentences.zh: 繼祖子甯，寧子復。

translations.literal: Jizu's son was Ning; Ning's son was Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu's son was Ning; Ning's son was Fu.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年詔曰：「太廟配享諸功臣，其贈王者，皆佐皇祖平定天下，有大功。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi an edict said: "The meritorious ministers who receive paired sacrifice in the Grand Temple, those posthumously made kings, all assisted the imperial ancestor in pacifying the realm and had great merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongzhi an edict said: "The meritorious ministers who receive paired sacrifice in the Grand Temple, those posthumously enfeoffed as kings, all aided the imperial ancestor in pacifying the realm with great merit.

sentences.zh: 而子孫或不沾寸祿，淪於氓隸。

translations.literal: Yet their descendants sometimes do not touch an inch of stipend and sink to commoner and bondservant status.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some of their descendants receive no stipend at all and sink to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 朕不忍，所司可求其世嫡，量授一官，奉先祀。」

translations.literal: We cannot bear it; the responsible offices may seek their hereditary legitimate heirs, grant one office in measure, and maintain ancestral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear this—the responsible offices shall find their legitimate heirs, grant them an office, and maintain ancestral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 乃自雲南召復，授南京錦衣衛世指揮使。

translations.literal: Fu was then summoned from Yunnan and appointed hereditary commandant of the Nanjing Brocade-Clad Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was summoned from Yunnan and appointed hereditary commandant of the Nanjing Brocade-Clad Guard.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年紹封四王后，封復孫玄振為懷遠侯，傳至曾孫延齡，有賢行。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing, after restoring enfeoffment of the four kings, Fu's grandson Xuanzhen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Huaiyuan; it passed to his great-grandson Yanling, who had worthy conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Jiajing, after the four kings' titles were restored, Fu's grandson Xuanzhen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Huaiyuan; the line passed to his great-grandson Yanling, a man of virtue.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年，全楚淪陷，延齡請統京兵赴九江協守。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen, all Chu fell; Yanling requested to command capital troops to go to Jiujiang to assist in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen, when all Chu fell, Yanling asked to lead capital troops to Jiujiang to help hold the line.

sentences.zh: 又言江都有地名常家沙，族丁數千皆其始祖遠裔，請鼓以忠義，練為親兵。

translations.literal: He also said that in Jiangdu there was a place called Chang Family Sandbar; several thousand clansmen were all distant descendants of their founding ancestor; he requested to rouse them with loyalty and righteousness and drill them as personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that near Jiangdu was a place called Chang Family Sandbar, where several thousand clansmen were distant descendants of the founder; he asked to rouse them with appeals to loyalty and train them as personal troops.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，不果行。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended it but it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan, but it was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 南都諸勳戚多恣睢自肆，獨延齡以守職稱。

translations.literal: Among the meritorious kin at the Southern Capital many were arrogant and self-indulgent; Yanling alone was praised for holding to his duties.
translations.idiomatic: At the Southern Capital most meritorious kin were arrogant and self-indulgent; Yanling alone was praised for doing his duty.

sentences.zh: 國亡，身自灌園，蕭然布衣終老。

translations.literal: When the state perished he personally watered gardens and ended his years plainly as a commoner in desolation.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty fell he watered his own garden and lived out his days plainly as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明太祖奮自滁陽，戡定四方，雖曰天授，蓋二王之力多焉。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Ming Taizu rose vigorously from Chuyang and conquered and settled the four quarters; though it is called Heaven's grant, largely the two kings' strength was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Ming Taizu rose from Chuyang and pacified the realm; though Heaven granted it, the two kings contributed most of the force.

sentences.zh: 中山持重有謀，功高不伐，自古名世之佐無以過之。

translations.literal: Zhongshan was weighty and had stratagem, his merit high yet not boastful—from antiquity aides who made an age renowned have had none to surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhongshan was grave and strategic, his merit great yet unboastful; no renowned minister of any age has surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 開平摧鋒陷陣，所向必克，智勇不在中山下；

translations.literal: Kaiping crushed the vanguard and stormed battle lines; wherever he advanced he must conquer; wisdom and courage were not below Zhongshan;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kaiping broke vanguards and stormed battle lines and was victorious wherever he marched; in wisdom and courage he was the equal of the Prince of Zhongshan;

sentences.zh: 而公忠謙遜，善持其功名，允為元勳之冠。

translations.literal: yet he was public-spirited, loyal, and modest, skilled at holding his merit and fame—truly the crown of the founding meritorious.
translations.idiomatic: yet he was loyal, public-spirited, and modest, and knew how to hold his fame—truly the foremost of the founding meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 身依日月，剖符錫土，若二王者，可謂極盛矣。

translations.literal: Their persons leaned on sun and moon; talismans were split and land bestowed—such as the two kings, one may say it was utmost flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: They stood beside the throne, received seals and fiefs—such honor for the two kings was the height of glory.

sentences.zh: 顧中山賞延後裔，世叨榮寵；

translations.literal: Yet Zhongshan's reward extended to posterity; generation after generation they enjoyed glory and favor;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Prince of Zhongshan's rewards extended to his descendants, who enjoyed honor for generations;

sentences.zh: 而開平天不假年，子孫亦復衰替。

translations.literal: while Kaiping Heaven did not grant years, and his descendants also declined and fell away.
translations.idiomatic: while Heaven did not grant the Prince of Kaiping long life, and his line declined.

sentences.zh: 貴匹勳齊，而食報或爽，其故何也？

translations.literal: Noble rank matched merit equally, yet eating the reward sometimes missed—what is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Their honors matched their merit, yet the rewards their lines received diverged—why was this?

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗語諸將曰：「為將不妄殺人，豈惟國家之利，爾子孫實受其福。」

translations.literal: The Founder once told the generals: "As a general do not kill people rashly—not only is it the state's benefit; your descendants in fact receive its blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder once told his generals: "A general who does not kill recklessly benefits not only the state—his descendants will reap the blessing.

sentences.zh: 信哉，可為為將帥者鑒矣。

translations.literal: Truly so—it may serve as a mirror for those who would be generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: How true this is—a lesson every commander should heed.
